read:gemm-core.summary: The EXL3 GEMM core is a cooperative-launch, persistent-grid fp16 tensor-core matmul over trellis-quantized weights. exl3_gemm.cu is a Torch-facing host wrapper that validates shapes, resolves suh/svh/A_had pointers, picks a kernel from a [K=1..8][cb=0..2][shape=1..4] instance table (or runs a runtime autotuner / a small-m GEMV fast path), and launches with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel at 90KB dynamic smem. exl3_gemm_kernel.cuh holds two __global__ kernels: exl3_gemm_kernel (single matrix) and exl3_mgemm_kernel (pointer-table multi-matrix for MoE/fused projections); both fully fuse the EXL3 incoherence processing — a grid-wide prologue applies diag(suh) then Hadamard-128 (x 1/sqrt(128)) from A into A_had, and the epilogue applies Hadamard-128, 1/sqrt(128) and diag(svh) (plus the MoE routing weight in mgemm) to the output, so the caller passes RAW activations and receives fully un-rotated outputs. exl3_gemm_inner.cuh is a Marlin-style 3-pipe (global->smem cp.async, smem->register ldmatrix+inline dequant, mma m16n8k16 fp16xfp16->fp32) inner loop with split-k across persistent blocks, reduced through a global lock/ticket protocol using partial sums staged in C itself (no separate reduction workspace). m is processed in chunks of exactly 16 rows (TILESIZE_M==16 always) with grid syncs between chunks. C is written as fp16 or fp32 (template c_fp32). The B-side dequant reuses exl3_dq.cuh dq_dispatch -> decode_3inst (codebook.cuh) and ptx.cuh MMA/cp.async/ldmatrix/barrier helpers, both already ported elsewhere.

symbols.name: exl3_gemm_kernel<bits, c_fp32, cb, TILESIZE_M, TILESIZE_K, TILESIZE_N, SH_STAGES, FRAG_STAGES>
symbols.contract: __global__ __launch_bounds__(256 * TILESIZE_K / 16) void exl3_gemm_kernel(const half* __restrict__ A, const uint16_t* __restrict__ B, void* __restrict__ C, const int size_m, const int size_k, const int size_n, int* __restrict__ locks, const half* __restrict__ suh, half* __restrict__ A_had, const half* __restrict__ svh). A: raw (un-rotated) row-major fp16 (m,k) contiguous. B: trellis, logically (k/16, n/16, 16*K) uint16, contiguous. C: (m,n) fp16 (c_fp32=false) or fp32 (c_fp32=true); does NOT need zeroing (first split-k block overwrites). locks: zeroed global int buffer, 1 int per output n-tile (index slice2_n), self-resetting. suh: fp16 vector length k (NOT k/16 — the host docstring's '(k//16)' describes the packed int16 su bitfield; the kernel reads ((half4*)suh)[lane] over full 128-element groups). A_had: fp16 scratch, size m*k, MAY alias A (in-place ok, prologue is separated by grid.sync). svh: fp16 vector length n. In this snapshot suh/svh/A_had are unconditionally dereferenced ('// if (suh)' commented out; epilogue always runs with post_scale=svh) => all three effectively REQUIRED. Launch: cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel, grid = dim3(num_sms) 1-D, num_sms = max(min(size_k/TILESIZE_K * size_n/TILESIZE_N, SM count),1); block = 256*TILESIZE_K/16 threads (shape1:256, shape2:512, shape3:512, shape4:256); dynamic smem = SMEM_MAX = 90*1024 always (requires cudaFuncSetAttribute(cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, SMEM_MAX) once per kernel per device). Body: (1) grid-strided warp prologue: for each 128-elem group of A, had_hf_r_128_inner<true,false>(A+off, A_had+off, suh + (off % size_k), 0.088388347648f) — pre-scale by suh then H128, scaled 1/sqrt(128); grid.sync(); A=A_had. (2) loop m in chunks of 16: exl3_gemm_kernel_inner<bits,c_fp32,cb,TM,TK,TN,SH_STAGES,FRAG_STAGES, shmem_out_had=true>(A_, B, C_, min(m,16), k, n, locks, svh); advance A_ by 16*k, C_ by 16*n; grid.sync() between chunks. Output Hadamard+svh is fused inside inner's epilogue (see exl3_gemm_kernel_inner). Constraints: k % TILESIZE_K == 0, n % TILESIZE_N == 0 (so k%16, n%128 minimum).
symbols.notes: Template instantiations that matter: bits(K) = 1..8, c_fp32 in {false,true}, cb in {0 (default 3INST),1 (mcg),2 (mul1)}, shapes 2,3,4 (shape 1 = (16,16,128,6,5) exists and IS selected by the Blackwell heuristic for K==2/4 && k<=2048 && !multi). Shapes: EXL3_GEMM_SHAPE_1 = 16,16,128,SH=6,FRAG=5; SHAPE_2 = 16,32,128,4,3; SHAPE_3 = 16,32,256,4,3; SHAPE_4 = 16,16,512,4,3.

symbols.name: exl3_mgemm_kernel<same template params>
symbols.contract: __global__ __launch_bounds__(256*TILESIZE_K/16) void exl3_mgemm_kernel(const half* A, const uint16_t** B_list, void* C, const int size_m, const int size_k, const int size_n, int* locks, const half** suh_list, half* A_had, const half** svh_list, int64_t* B_indices, half* B_weights, const int bszm_in, const int bszm_out, const int min_index, const int max_index, const int num_tokens, const int* size_n_list, void** C_list). B_list/suh_list/svh_list: device arrays of device pointers (host passes at::kLong tensors of addresses; kernel arg is the pointer-table base). Slot j (j in 0..bszm-1, bszm = max(bszm_in,bszm_out)) selects q = B_indices ? B_indices[j] : j; negative q skips the slot (scratch untouched). A: fp16 [bszm_in, m, k]; if bszm_in==1, A[0] is broadcast but re-transformed per slot. A_had: fp16 scratch >= bszm*m*k elements (kernel writes slab A_had + j*m*k per slot; undersize = silent OOB). C: [bszm_out, m, n] fp16/fp32; with B_weights != null, C doubles as per-expert scratch and the final reduction sums each token-group's stride = bszm/num_tokens contiguous slots into C[t] (t = token index); only rows C[0..num_tokens) are the results. B_weights: fp16 parallel to indices; folded into the output epilogue scale (scale = 1/sqrt(128) * weights[j]). min_index/max_index: expert-range filter for EP shards; at num_tokens==1 indices are compacted (via __device__ globals v_indices[128]/v_weights[128]/bszm_sync, done by thread (0,0,0) then __threadfence + grid.sync), at num_tokens>1 out-of-range slots are masked to -1 in place, preserving slot->token grouping. Capacity: MAX_INDICES 128 slots. size_n_list/C_list: optional per-matrix output widths + output pointers (n_j = size_n_list[q], C_ = C_list[q]); then size_n is only the MAX width for lock sizing; host forbids combining with num_tokens>1/filtering/weights. Launch: cooperative, grid = dim3(num_sms, 1, concurrency); host computes num_sms = tiles (=k/TK * n/TN); if num_sms*bszm > total_sms -> max(total_sms/bszm,1); if tiles/num_sms > 48 -> min(total_sms, num_sms*2); concurrency = min(total_sms/num_sms, bszm); block dim per shape table; smem = SMEM_MAX. Slots strided over blockIdx.z: for (i=0; i<bszm; i+=gridDim.z) j = i + blockIdx.z. Per-slot: suh-Hadamard prologue into A_had+j*m*k, barrier, inner matmul with shmem_out_had=false and post_scale=nullptr, locks base = locks + blockIdx.z * size_n/128 per z-slice, barrier, then epilogue pass in-place over C_: had_ff_r_128_inner<false,true> (fp32) or had_hf_r_128_inner<false,true> (fp16) with svh_list[q] and scale = 0.088388347648f * (B_weights ? weights[j] : 1). On __CUDA_ARCH__ > 890 (incl. sm_121a) inter-stage syncs use group_barrier(blockIdx.z, gridDim.x, locks + BARRIER_LOCKS_OFFSET) instead of full grid.sync, so z-groups run decoupled; the index-compaction sync and pre-reduction sync still use grid.sync().
symbols.notes: Final reduction (B_weights path, blockIdx.z==0 only): per column col of the m*n block, for each token t: sum C[(t*stride + j)*m*n + col] over j in 0..stride where slot active (B_indices[t*stride+j] >= 0 or no indices), write to C[t*m*n + col]; groups processed in increasing t (aliasing-safe as commented). Requires size_m*size_n % 32 == 0. v_indices/v_weights/bszm_sync are module-scope __device__ globals — one in-flight filtered mgemm per device module (stream-serialized in practice).

symbols.name: exl3_gemm_kernel_inner<bits, c_fp32, cb, TILESIZE_M, TILESIZE_K, TILESIZE_N, SH_STAGES, FRAG_STAGES, shmem_out_had>
symbols.contract: inline __device__ void exl3_gemm_kernel_inner(const half* A, const uint16_t* B, void* C, const int size_m (<=16), const int size_k, const int size_n, int* locks, const half* post_scale). The whole compute core. Derived constants: TILEBLOCKS_K = TILESIZE_K/16; TILEBLOCKS_N = TILESIZE_N/16; FRAGS_N_PER_WARP = 2*TILEBLOCKS_N/(256/32); sh_a_stage_size = TILESIZE_M*TILESIZE_K halves; sh_b_stage_size = TILEBLOCKS_K*TILEBLOCKS_N*(256/16)*bits uint16s (16*bits uint16 per 16x16 tile); sh_c_size = max(4*256*FRAGS_N_PER_WARP, shmem_out_had ? TILESIZE_N*TILESIZE_M : 0) floats. static_assert SMEM_MAX >= SH_STAGES*(2*sh_a + 2*sh_b) + 4*sh_c. smem layout: [sh_a stages | sh_b stages | sh_c]. Threads: t = threadIdx.x % 256; sub_k = threadIdx.x / 256 (k-split within block, TILESIZE_K/16 sub-slices); 8 warps of the base 256 threads own FRAGS_N_PER_WARP n-fragments each. A smem is XOR-swizzled: A_COLS = TILESIZE_K/8 int4 cols; SWIZZLE_MASK = A_COLS-1; SWIZZLE_SHIFT = (A_COLS<=2)?2:1; col_sw = col ^ ((row >> SHIFT) & MASK); fragments loaded via ldsm4 (ldmatrix x4). B fragments produced by dq_dispatch<bits,cb>(shb, lane_id << 3, frag0, frag1) directly in mma column layout — no ldmatrix on B. Persistent-block work split: slices over tiles_k*tiles_n tile space, k-major (index_k = slice_i % tiles_k, index_n = slice_i / tiles_k); block b covers [tiles*b/gridDim.x, tiles*(b+1)/gridDim.x). Three software pipes (global->smem via cp_async 16B + commit_group/wait_group<SH_STAGES-2>, smem->frag double/multi-buffered FRAG_STAGES 1..5 via unrolled FSTAGE macros, mma). MMA: ptx_mma_m16n8k16 fp16xfp16+fp32->fp32 (EXL3_GEMM_H_ACC fp16-accum variant is sm_86-only; 0 on sm_121a). Split-k reduction at each column boundary (slice2_k == tiles_k-1 or slice end): threadblock_reduce() folds sub_k accumulators through sh_c (explicit store/add schedule per TILEBLOCKS_K in {2,3,4}; a lighter store_small path when size_m <= 8); then global protocol on lock = &locks[slice2_n]: lock_i = tiles_k - slice2_k - 1 (blocks within a column retire in REVERSE k order), lock_d = number of k-tiles covered; barrier_acquire(lock, lock_i) spins on ld.global.acquire.gpu until *lock == lock_i; non-first blocks read_sum_gl() (add C partial from global, fp16 read via half2->float2); non-last blocks write_sum_gl() partial to C; last block: if shmem_out_had, write_sum_tile_sh() (fp32 tile to sh_c row-major TILESIZE_N stride) + __syncthreads + output_had_sh_gl(): per 128-col group, had_ff_r_128_inner<false,true> (fp32 C) or had_fh_r_128_inner<false,true> (fp16 C) from sh_c to global C with post_scale = svh + slice2_n*TILESIZE_N + col*128 and r_scale = 0.088388347648f; else plain write_sum_gl. barrier_release(lock, lock_d, last): last resets *lock = 0 (self-resetting), else fence.acq_rel.gpu + red.relaxed.gpu.global.add.
symbols.notes: Partial split-k sums are staged IN C ITSELF (in C's dtype — fp16 C loses some precision on multi-block columns; fp32 C avoids this). No separate reduction workspace. locks must be zeroed once at allocation only.

symbols.name: EXL3_GEMM_ARGS / EXL3_MGEMM_ARGS / EXL3_GEMM_T_ARGS
symbols.contract: EXL3_GEMM_ARGS = (const half* A, const uint16_t* B, void* C, const int size_m, const int size_k, const int size_n, int* locks, const half* suh, half* A_had, const half* svh). EXL3_MGEMM_ARGS = (const half* A, const uint16_t** B_list, void* C, const int size_m, const int size_k, const int size_n, int* locks, const half** suh_list, half* A_had, const half** svh_list, int64_t* B_indices, half* B_weights, const int bszm_in, const int bszm_out, const int min_index, const int max_index, const int num_tokens, const int* size_n_list, void** C_list). EXL3_GEMM_T_ARGS = (const int bits, const bool c_fp32, const int cb, const int TILESIZE_M, const int TILESIZE_K, const int TILESIZE_N, const int SH_STAGES, const int FRAG_STAGES). Typedefs fp_exl3_gemm_kernel / fp_exl3_mgemm_kernel are function pointers over these arg lists.
symbols.notes: size_m here is the TOTAL row count (kernel loops in 16-row chunks internally), not <=16.

symbols.name: exl3_gemm / exl3_gemm_gr
symbols.contract: int exl3_gemm(const at::Tensor& A, const at::Tensor& B, at::Tensor& C, optional suh, optional A_had, optional svh, int force_shape_idx, bool mcg, bool mul1, int force_num_sms) -> shape_idx used (0 = no kernel, 90 = gemv path took it). Computes size_m = prod(A.dims[:-1]), size_k = A.size(-1), size_n = B.size(1)*16, K = B.size(2)/16; cb = mcg?1 : mul1?2 : 0 (both set = error). Order of dispatch: (1) optional int8-GEMV experimental path (mul1 + env EXL3_INT8_GEMV=1, m small); (2) exl3_gemv_try_launch small-m QTIP-style GEMV (same kernelArgs layout) when no force flags and suh&&A_had&&svh; (3) runtime autotuner (CoopKernelAutotuner, keyed by hash of min(roundup_pow2(m),16), k, n, K, c_fp32, device, cc, num_sms, cb) over all compatible shapes; (4) static fallback select_exl3_gemm_kernel + cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel(kernel, num_sms, block_dim, kernelArgs, SMEM_MAX, stream). kernelArgs order (graph-patchable indices): 0=A,1=B,2=C,3=size_m,4=size_k,5=size_n,6=locks,7=suh,8=A_had,9=svh.
symbols.notes: Requires cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, 90KB) once per kernel pointer per device (cached in kernel_attr_set).

symbols.name: exl3_mgemm / exl3_mgemm_gr
symbols.contract: int exl3_mgemm(A [bszm_in,m,k] fp16, B int64 ptr-table [num_matrices], C [bszm_out,m,n] fp16/fp32, suh int64 ptr-table, svh int64 ptr-table, optional indices int64 [*,num_indices], optional weights fp16 [*,num_indices], int K, int force_shape_idx, mcg, mul1, int min_index, int max_index, int force_num_sms, int num_tokens=1, optional size_n_list int32, optional c_ptrs int64) -> shape_idx. bszm_in = A.size(0), bszm_out = C.size(0) (or c_ptrs.size(0)); both clamped to num_indices; bszm = max. Host MUST validate A_had.numel() >= bszm*m*k. K is passed explicitly (B is just addresses, no shape). kernelArgs order: 0=A,1=B_list,2=C,3=size_m,4=size_k,5=size_n,6=locks,7=suh_list,8=A_had,9=svh_list,10=indices,11=weights,12=bszm_in,13=bszm_out,14=min_index,15=max_index,16=num_tokens,17=size_n_list,18=c_ptrs. Grid: dim3(num_sms,1,concurrency) as computed in the mgemm launch code (see mgemm kernel entry). Limitations: k%16==0, n%128==0, <=128 slots with range filtering.
symbols.notes: Modes: multi-in/multi-out (A[j]@B[q]->C[j]); broadcast one input (bszm_in==1) for fused gate/up or MoE fan-out; weighted MoE reduce into per-token rows; EP shard filtering via min/max_index with local pointer tables.

symbols.name: select_gemm_shape
symbols.contract: int select_gemm_shape(int cc, int size_m, int size_k, int size_n, int K, bool multi, int bszm_in, int bszm_out). Multiplies size_k *= bszm_in, size_n *= bszm_out before deciding. CC_BLACKWELL (== CC_HOPPER branch): if ((K==4||K==2) && !multi && size_k<=2048) return 1; if K>=7: {mod256 && n<=8192 -> (k>32768 ? 3 : 2); mod512 && n>32768 -> 4; else 2}; else: {mod256 && n<=4096 -> (k>8192 && K>=3 ? 3 : 2); mod512 && n>16384 -> 4; mod256 -> 3; else 2}.
symbols.notes: cc mapping (exl3_devctx.cu): prop.major >= 10 -> CC_BLACKWELL(5). GB10 sm_121 major=12 -> CC_BLACKWELL. On the autotune path this heuristic is bypassed entirely.

symbols.name: exl3_gemm_shape_compat
symbols.contract: bool exl3_gemm_shape_compat(int shape_idx, int size_m, int size_k, int size_n, int K): (size_k % tilesize_k[shape] == 0) && (size_n % tilesize_n[shape] == 0). Tables: tilesize_k = {0,16,32,32,16}, tilesize_n = {0,128,128,256,512}, blockdim = {0,256,512,512,256} (index 0 unused).

symbols.name: select_exl3_gemm_kernel / select_exl3_mgemm_kernel / get_gemm_kernel_ptr / get_mgemm_kernel_ptr
symbols.contract: Lookup into static tables tab_gemm_fp32/tab_gemm_fp16/tab_mgemm_fp32/tab_mgemm_fp16 [K:1..8][cb:0..2] -> per-shape instance array [0..4] (index 0 = nullptr). select_* also outputs block_dim = blockdim[shape] and clamps num_sms: gemm: *num_sms = max(min(k/tk * n/tn, *num_sms), 1); mgemm: *num_sms = min(k/tk * n/tn / (*num_sms > 128 ? 20 : 24), *num_sms) — but the mgemm host then recomputes num_sms/concurrency itself (tiles cap, /bszm, x2 if >48 tiles per SM slice).

symbols.name: DevCtx (exl3_devctx)
symbols.contract: Per-device singleton: get_num_sms(dev) (cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount), get_cc(dev) (CC_* enum), get_locks(dev) -> int* lock buffer cudaMalloc'd + cudaMemset(0) once, size (MAX_TILES_C + 2*MAX_BARRIERS + MOE_SCHED_INTS)*4 bytes = (1048576 + 2048 + 66)*4 ≈ 4.19 MB; get_ws(dev) -> 16MB scratch (WORKSPACE_SIZE, NOT used by the GEMM path — used by gemv/other). Constants: MAX_TILES_C = 1024*1024 (split-k column locks, indexed slice2_n [+ blockIdx.z*size_n/128 in mgemm]); MAX_BARRIERS = 1024; BARRIER_LOCKS_OFFSET = MAX_TILES_C (group_barrier counter+sense pairs, 2 ints per z-group); MOE_SCHED_OFFSET = MAX_TILES_C + 2*MAX_BARRIERS, MOE_SCHED_INTS = 66 (MoE scheduler tickets, used by other kernels).
symbols.notes: Host contract: allocate + zero ONCE per device; all protocols (split-k ticket lock, group_barrier sense-reversing counter) self-reset, so nothing must be zeroed between calls. Concurrent kernels on different streams sharing one lock buffer would collide — ExLlamaV3 relies on single-stream serialization.

symbols.name: dq_dispatch<bits, cb> (exl3_dq.cuh)
symbols.contract: __device__ void dq_dispatch(const uint32_t* ptr, int idx = lane_id*8, FragB& frag0, FragB& frag1): decode 8 consecutive trellis codes of one 16x16 tile (256 codes = 16*bits uint16s) into two mma B fragments (each Vec<half2,2>). Per-bits specializations: 1 bit dq8_aligned_1bit, 2 dq8_aligned_2bits, 3 dq8<3,cb,4>, 4 dq8_aligned_4bits (FSHF_IMM/BFE16_IMM), 5/6/8 dq4 x2, 7 dq2x2 x2. All bottom out in decode_3inst_2<cb> (codebook.cuh — already ported).
symbols.notes: REUSED, ported elsewhere per task statement. Bit-stream origin: code word w for flat tile index t occupies bits [(t+257)*bits - 16, (t+257)*bits) of the tile's 256*bits-bit stream, wrapped mod 256*bits (the % (bits*256/32) index wrap).

symbols.name: had_hf_r_128_inner<pre_scale, post_scale> / had_ff_r_128_inner / had_fh_r_128_inner (hadamard_inner.cuh)
symbols.contract: One-warp 128-element Hadamard transform: (const T_in* input_ptr, T_out* output_ptr, const half* scale, const float r_scale). Variants: hf = half->half, ff = float->float, fh = float->half. pre_scale multiplies input by scale[i] before H; post_scale multiplies after. Internally fp32 (4-elem butterfly + shuffle_had_f4x32/f2x32 warp shuffles). Scale indexing uses (blockIdx.y*32 + lane) — blockIdx.y is always 0 in GEMM launches, so scale points at the current 128-group's slice. r_scale = 0.088388347648f = 1/sqrt(128) throughout. In/out may alias.
symbols.notes: REUSED (shared with standalone had_r_128 op); needs half4 type (struct of 2 half2, from compat.cuh).

symbols.name: ptx.cuh helpers
symbols.contract: REUSED, ported elsewhere: FragA=Vec<half2,4>, FragB=Vec<half2,2>, FragC=Vec<float,4>, FragC_h=Vec<half2,2>; ptx_mma_m16n8k16 (f32 and f16 accum overloads); barrier_acquire(int* lock, int stage) (thread-0 spin on ld.global.acquire.gpu.b32 + __syncthreads); barrier_release(int* lock, int val, bool reset) (reset -> *lock=0, else fence.acq_rel.gpu + red.relaxed.gpu.global.add.s32); cp_async (16B cp.async.cg), cp_async_fence, cp_async_wait<n>, ldsm4 (ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n8.x4.shared.b16); group_barrier(group_id, group_size, int* counters) sense-reversing per-z-group barrier with __nanosleep(32) backoff; fshift/bfe64/FSHF_IMM/BFE16_IMM.
symbols.notes: cp_async_pred is documented as MISCOMPILING when built for Blackwell — the kernels use `if (pred) cp_async(...)` instead; keep that form in the port.

symbols.name: SMEM_MAX / EXL3_GEMM_BASE_THREADS
symbols.contract: #define EXL3_GEMM_BASE_THREADS 256; #define SMEM_MAX (90*1024) — every launch passes SMEM_MAX as dynamic smem regardless of actual need (sized for the largest shape at K=8; e.g. shape2 K=8: 4 stages * (16*32*2B A + 2*8*16*8*2B... = sh_a 1KB + sh_b 8KB) = 36KB + sh_c 16KB).

dependencies: Torch-coupled (replace in port): ATen/c10 tensor args, TORCH_CHECK* macros (util.h), at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream, OptionalCUDAGuard, OPTPTR — all host-side only; the __global__ kernels themselves are pure CUDA and freestanding
graph.cuh Graph / record_param (GP_gemm_* / GP_mgemm_* arg-index recording for CUDA-graph pointer patching) — replace with Atlas graph plumbing or drop

coop_autotune.cuh CoopKernelAutotuner / CoopAutotuneCandidate (NOT in ref dir) — runtime autotuner over (kernel, block_dim, num_sms) candidates; replaceable by the static select_gemm_shape heuristic for a first port
exl3_gemv.cuh / exl3_gemv_int8.cuh small-m fast paths (separate kernels, same 10-slot kernelArgs layout; dispatched before the GEMM) — optional for a first port
exl3_dq.cuh -> codebook.cuh decode_3inst/decode_3inst_2 (already ported elsewhere)
ptx.cuh (already ported elsewhere): Frag types, mma, cp.async, ldsm4, barrier_acquire/release, group_barrier
hadamard_inner.cuh: had_hf_r_128_inner / had_ff_r_128_inner / had_fh_r_128_inner + shuffle_had_* (freestanding CUDA; needs half4 from compat.cuh)
exl3_devctx: per-device lock buffer (freestanding: cudaMalloc + memset once), SM count, CC enum
cooperative_groups (cg::this_grid().sync()) + cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel driver support
Module-scope __device__ globals in exl3_gemm_kernel.cuh: v_indices[128], v_weights[128], bszm_sync (mgemm index filtering)
read:gemm-core.dtype_notes: Everything user-visible is fp16-in: A must be fp16 contiguous (host TORCH_CHECK_DTYPE(A, kHalf)); B trellis uint16; suh/svh fp16 (full-length k and n vectors of signs; the '(k//16)' in the docstrings describes the PACKED int16 su/sv bitfields, not what the kernel reads). C is fp16 OR fp32, selected by the c_fp32 template parameter from C's dtype — both variants are compiled for every (K, cb, shape). Accumulation: mma m16n8k16 fp16xfp16 -> fp32 accumulators (FragC float4); the fp16-accumulate variant (EXL3_GEMM_H_ACC, FragC_h) is compiled ONLY for __CUDA_ARCH__ == 860, so on sm_121a accumulation is always fp32. Hadamard transforms compute in fp32 internally regardless of storage dtype. Split-k partials are staged in C's own dtype: with fp16 C, inter-block read_sum_gl/write_sum_gl round through fp16 per partial (small precision loss on multi-block k columns); with fp32 C they stay fp32. mgemm final MoE reduction likewise sums in __hadd (fp16) for fp16 C and float for fp32 C. No bf16 anywhere. For Atlas: convert BF16 activations to fp16 before the kernel (exact for post-norm magnitudes; could be fused into the suh-Hadamard prologue by adding a bf16-in variant of had_hf_r_128_inner), and prefer c_fp32=true when feeding the FP32 residual highway — that also upgrades split-k partials and the MoE reduction to fp32 for free.

read:gemv-core.dtype_notes: Entirely fp16-centric. Inputs: A must be fp16 (TORCH_CHECK_DTYPE(A, kHalf)); B is int16 trellis words reinterpreted as uint32; suh/svh/A_had are fp16. Output C is fp16 OR fp32, selected by the c_fp32 template bool (both instantiated for every bits/cb/MMODE/CFG combo); fp16 C stored via __float2half_rn, fp32 C stored raw. Accumulation: the MMA is fp16-in/fp16-accumulate (mma...f16.f16.f16.f16 into FragC_h), deliberately folded into a per-thread float2 accumulator on a fixed cadence — every FOLD MMAs (FOLD=4 narrow / 2 wide, i.e. every 64 or 32 k-elements of fp16 accumulation) via __low2float/__high2float, then the fp16 frag is zeroed. Cross-warp reduction and output are pure fp32 (sh_red float smem). Hadamard stages compute internally in fp32 (shuffle_had_f4x32/f2x32 on floats) with fp16 load/round-trip for the half variants; the fp32-C epilogue (had_ff_r_128_inner) keeps everything fp32 with fp16 svh scales. The mul1/mcg decode depends on fp16 bit tricks: __dp4a(x,0x01010101,0x6400) builds a biased fp16 bit pattern, k_inv=0x1eee, k_bias=0xc931 as half — these constants are fp16-only and MUST NOT be naively converted to bf16. No bf16 anywhere in ExLlamaV3. For Atlas BF16 serving: convert activations bf16->fp16 at the input-Hadamard stage (add a had_bf16-in/fp16-out variant of had_hf_r_128_inner — it already goes through fp32 internally, so the change is two load/convert lines), and for BF16/FP32-residual output prefer c_fp32=true + a bf16-writing variant of had_ff_r_128_inner (fp32 sums -> H128 -> svh -> __float2bfloat16). Keep the decode math and MMA in fp16 verbatim; only the vector I/O dtype at the two Hadamard boundaries changes.

Output Hadamard mutates C in place after all groups complete; with the split port the epilogue kernel must be ordered after the matmul on the same stream (trivial) but must also cover exactly m*n/128 warps or tail columns keep un-rotated garbage.

MMODE=1 rounds all M in 2..8 through ROWS=8 smem (sh_red 16KB narrow config) — occupancy on GB10 should be re-checked; upstream caches occupancy per kernel pointer, port must too or pay a driver query per launch.

read:gemv-core.summary: The EXL3 GEMV path is a QTIP-style small-M (M<=8) fused kernel for trellis-quantized matmul at 2/3/4 bpw. It is launched cooperatively (cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel) with the exact same 10-argument signature as exl3_gemm_kernel, and fuses the ENTIRE data path in one kernel: a grid-strided input stage applies diag(suh) then Hadamard-128 to A (writing a rotated copy into the A_had scratch buffer), grid.sync, then warps split K with no further synchronization — B trellis words stream straight to registers via __ldcs behind a compile-time prefetch ring, two-word bit windows are resolved in-warp by lane shuffles (or optional smem staging), decoded through the procedural codebook (3INST/MCG/MUL1), and multiplied via one m16n8k16 fp16-accumulate MMA pair per 16x16 tile with periodic fp32 folding; per-block cross-warp reduction goes through shared memory to C, then a final grid.sync and an output stage applies Hadamard-128 then diag(svh) to C in place (fp16 or fp32 C). Two configs exist: narrow (CFG 0: 512 threads, 16 k-split warps, 2 n-tiles/warp, 32 output cols/block) and wide (CFG 1: 256 threads, 8 k-splits, 4 n-tiles/warp, 64 cols), plus MMODE 0 (M==1 fast path) and MMODE 1 (2<=M<=8 with row-guarded loads). Above M=8, or when shape/heuristic checks fail, the caller falls through to the block-pipelined exl3_gemm kernel. The arch gate excluding non-Ampere is commented out, so Blackwell currently takes this path per-bits (always for 2 bpw; narrow-envelope shapes for 3/4 bpw), using the lane-shuffle extraction (SMEM_STAGE=false) by default.

symbols.name: exl3_gemv_kernel
symbols.contract: template <int bits, bool c_fp32, int cb, int MMODE, int CFG, bool SMEM_STAGE> __global__ __launch_bounds__(CFG==0?512:256) void exl3_gemv_kernel(EXL3_GEMM_ARGS) where EXL3_GEMM_ARGS = (const half* __restrict__ A, const uint16_t* __restrict__ B, void* __restrict__ C, const int size_m, const int size_k, const int size_n, int* __restrict__ locks, const half* __restrict__ suh, half* __restrict__ A_had, const half* __restrict__ svh). Template params: bits in {2,3,4} (static_assert); cb in {0,1,2} = 3INST/MCG/MUL1 codebook; MMODE 0 = m==1 fast path (only lanes<4 load A rows), MMODE 1 = 2<=m<=EXL3_GEMV_MAX_M(8) with row guard r0<size_m; CFG 0 'narrow' (WK=16 k-split warps, WNT=2 n-tiles/warp, PF=4 prefetch ring, FOLD=4, 512 threads, COLS=32), CFG 1 'wide' (WK=8, WNT=4, PF=2, FOLD=2, 256 threads, COLS=64); SMEM_STAGE false = lane-shuffle window extraction (default), true = stage tile words in warp-private smem then use register dq. Launch: cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel, grid = dim3(MIN(size_n/COLS, occupancy_blocks_per_sm*num_sms)) 1-D, block = dim3(512|256), dynamic smem 0. Static smem: __shared__ float sh_red[WK][ROWS][COLS] (ROWS = MMODE==0?1:8) = narrow 2KB(M1)/16KB(M8), wide 2KB/16KB; plus SMEM_STAGE staging WK*LOADS*LSTRIDE u32 (bits4 narrow: 16*2*32*4=4KB). Derived constants: TWORDS=8*bits u32 per 16x16 tile; LOADS = bits==2 ? WNT/2 : WNT; LSTRIDE = bits==3 ? 24 : 32; slice_stride = (size_n/16)*TWORDS u32 (B viewed as u32[k/16][n/16][8*bits]); B pointer per warp: B32 + ks0*slice_stride + group*WNT*TWORDS + lane, loaded __ldcs (bits==3: lanes<24 only). k is chunked: chunk=CEIL_DIVIDE(size_k/16, WK), warp w owns slices [w*chunk, w*chunk+myn). A read as half2 rows: lane covers row lane>>2, a_col=(ks0+i)*8+(lane&3) and +4; a01[1]=a23[1]=zero (rows 8-15 of the m16 tile always zero => M<=8). Requires suh/A_had/svh non-null, size_k%128==0, size_n%128==0. locks is UNUSED (cross-block sync = exactly two cooperative_groups grid.sync(): after input Hadamard, before output Hadamard).
symbols.notes: Body phases: (1) input stage, grid-strided over size_m*size_k/128 warps: had_hf_r_128_inner<true,false>(A+w*128, A_had+w*128, suh+(w*128)%size_k, 0.088388347648f /*1/sqrt(128)*/); grid.sync(); A=A_had. (2) main loop over output column groups (group = blockIdx.x; group < size_n/COLS; group += gridDim.x): prefetch ring pf[PF][LOADS] (indices compile-time or pf spills), per k-slice: shuffle/stage words, decode 2 FragB per tile, mma_ab_h twice per tile into FragC_h ch[WNT][2], fold ch->float2 acc0 when (d+1)%FOLD==0 or last; then sh_red[warp][row][col]=acc0, __syncthreads, all threads sum over WK warps and store C (fp32 raw or __float2half_rn), __syncthreads. (3) grid.sync(); output stage grid-strided over size_m*size_n/128 warps: c_fp32 ? had_ff_r_128_inner<false,true>(C+w*128, C+w*128, svh+(w*128)%size_n, 1/sqrt(128)) : had_hf_r_128_inner<false,true>(same). Complete data path: y = ((x .* suh) H128/sqrt128) @ W_hat, then (y H128/sqrt128) .* svh — both rotations fully fused in-kernel; the kernel reads RAW activations.

read:dispatch-devctx.summary: This subsystem is the host-side dispatch/selection layer plus per-device context for EXL3's cooperative trellis GEMM kernels. exl3_kernel_map.cu holds static function-pointer tables `tab_gemm_{fp16,fp32}[9][3]` and `tab_mgemm_{fp16,fp32}[9][3]` indexed [K=1..8][cb=0..2], each entry an array of 5 pointers indexed by shape_idx (0 = nullptr, shapes 1-4), and a per-arch heuristic `select_gemm_shape` that picks one of 4 fixed tile shapes from (K, size_k, size_n, divisibility of n by 256/512, multi flag). exl3_devctx.cu is a mutex-guarded process singleton caching per-device SM count, a 5-level compute-capability class (major>=10 => CC_BLACKWELL, which covers sm_121a), a ~4.2 MB zero-initialized "locks" buffer used for split-k spinlocks + group barriers + a MoE scheduler region, and a lazily allocated 16 MB generic workspace (unused by the GEMM path in these files). exl3_gemm.cu shows the launch contract the tables assume: all kernels are launched with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel, always with dynamic smem = SMEM_MAX = 90 KB (opted in once per (kernel, device) via cudaFuncSetAttribute, memoized in `std::set<void*> kernel_attr_set[MAX_DEVICES]`), grid = (num_sms, 1[, concurrency for mgemm]), block = 256 * TILESIZE_K/16 threads. By default (no forced shape/SM count) upstream does NOT use the heuristic at all: it enumerates every compatible shape 1..4 and hands them to a `CoopKernelAutotuner` keyed by an FNV hash of (m rounded to pow2 capped 16, k, n, K, c_fp32, device, cc, sms, cb[, bszm_in/out capped 24]); the heuristic is the fallback for forced launches and graph capture.

symbols.name: select_gemm_shape
symbols.contract: int select_gemm_shape(int cc, int size_m, int size_k, int size_n, int K, bool multi, int bszm_in, int bszm_out) — returns shape_idx 1..4 (0 = no kernel). NOTE: header prototype in exl3_kernel_map.cuh is stale (declares `int bits, bool multi` only); the .cu definition adds bszm_in/bszm_out which scale size_k/size_n before the switch (`size_k *= bszm_in; size_n *= bszm_out;`). size_m is ignored. CC_BLACKWELL shares the CC_HOPPER branch verbatim: `if ((K == 4 || K == 2) && !multi) { if (size_k <= 2048) return 1; } if (K >= 7) { if (mod_256 && size_n <= 8192) return size_k > 32768 ? 3 : 2; if (mod_512 && size_n > 32768) return 4; return 2; } if (mod_256 && size_n <= 4096) return size_k > 8192 && K >= 3 ? 3 : 2; if (mod_512 && size_n > 16384) return 4; if (mod_256) return 3; return 2;` where mod_256 = (size_n % 256 == 0) BEFORE the bszm scaling, mod_512 likewise.
symbols.notes: Blackwell reachability: shape 1 only for K in {2,4}, single-gemm (!multi), size_k<=2048; shapes 2/3/4 reachable for every K 1..8. mgemm (multi=true) never picks shape 1 via the heuristic. shape 2 is the universal fallback (only requires n%128==0).

read:dispatch-devctx.dtype_notes: A is ALWAYS fp16 (TORCH_CHECK_DTYPE(A, kHalf)); there is no bf16 variant anywhere in this layer — Atlas must convert BF16 activations to FP16 (and back) around the call, or add bf16 kernel instantiations itself. B is uint16 trellis codes (kShort), K = B.size(2)/16 bits per weight. suh/svh are fp16 sign/scale vectors (per-16 packed rows: suh shape k/16, svh shape n/16 in the tensor API comment, though the kernel indexes them per-element modulo size_k/size_n — they are expanded sign vectors at device level). C is void*: the ONLY dtype switch is the `bool c_fp32` template parameter, chosen at the host from `C.dtype() == at::kFloat`, selecting tab_*_fp32 vs tab_*_fp16. fp32 tables mean C is written (and, in split-k, spilled/re-read through global) as float; fp16 tables write half, and the mgemm weighted MoE reduction then also sums in HALF (`half sum; sum = __hadd(sum, *C___)`) — a precision reason upstream MoE uses fp32 C (py_mlp interm_dtype == torch.float). Internal MMA accumulation is fp32 in both variants on Blackwell (the fp16-accumulate EXL3_GEMM_H_ACC path is gated to __CUDA_ARCH__ == 860 exactly and never compiles for sm_121a). Hadamard scale constant 0.088388347648f = 1/sqrt(128) is applied on input; output side applies 1/sqrt(128) (times MoE routing weight in mgemm) fused with svh. For an Atlas BF16 engine the cheapest correct integration: BF16->FP16 cast into the A buffer, run kernel with c_fp32=true, read fp32 C into the BF16/FP32 residual path.
read:dispatch-devctx.blackwell_notes: CC classification: prop.major >= 10 => CC_BLACKWELL = 5 (sm_121a/GB10 qualifies; note sm_120/121 have major 12 — still >= 10). CC_BLACKWELL and CC_HOPPER share one branch in select_gemm_shape, so a Blackwell-only port hard-codes that branch. Heuristically reachable shapes on Blackwell: gemm => shape 1 only when (K==2 || K==4) && size_k<=2048, shapes 2/3/4 for all K; mgemm (multi=true) => shapes 2/3/4 only. BUT the default upstream path is the autotuner, which tries EVERY compatible shape 1..4 for every K — so the minimal instantiation matrix for a Blackwell-only port that keeps autotuning is: exl3_gemm_kernel and exl3_mgemm_kernel for K=1..8 x cb in {1 (mcg), 2 (mul1)} x shapes {1,2,3,4} x c_fp32 in {false,true} (cb0 legacy 3INST optional; shape 1 for mgemm and for K not in {2,4} may be dropped if only the heuristic is used, and shape 1 gemm may be dropped for K not in {2,4}). That is 8*2*4*2 = 128 gemm + 128 mgemm instantiations full, or 8*2*3*2 + extra-shape-1-for-K2/K4 = ~104+8 if heuristic-only. Device-code arch gates: __CUDA_ARCH__ > 890 switches mgemm from grid.sync() to the cheaper group_barrier (atomic counter+sense in locks[MAX_TILES_C..]) for per-z-slice syncs — active on sm_121a; grid.sync() still used for index packing and pre-reduction, so cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel is REQUIRED (grid.x*grid.z <= SM count at 1 block/SM occupancy given 90KB dynamic smem). EXL3_GEMM_H_ACC is OFF on sm_121a (== 860 only). ptx.cuh warns cp_async_pred 'produces incorrect code when compiling for Blackwell' — kernels use `if (...) cp_async(...)` instead; keep that pattern. Smem: always request 90KB dynamic (cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize once per kernel) — fits sm_121a's 99KB opt-in; do not raise it, the tile static_asserts assume 90KB. GB10 has few SMs relative to datacenter parts, so the mgemm concurrency computation (concurrency = MIN(total_sms/num_sms, bszm)) matters for MoE fan-out throughput.

B_list, suh_list, svh_list, indices, weights, bszm_in, bszm_out, min_index, max_index, num_tokens, size_n_list, c_list). Wrap with a BF16<->FP16 cast pair on the Atlas side (A cast in, C either fp32 direct or fp16 cast out). risks: Cooperative launch: grid must fit co-resident (1 block/SM at 90KB smem). GB10 has a small SM count; the mgemm grid formula divides SMs by bszm — with many experts (bszm up to 128) num_sms collapses to total_sms/bszm and per-matrix parallelism gets thin. read:hadamard.summary: This subsystem implements the 128-point Hadamard "incoherence" rotations that bracket every EXL3 packed matmul: y_seg = post ⊙ ((pre ⊙ x_seg) · H128 · (scale/√128)) applied independently to each contiguous 128-element segment of each row. The transform is decomposed as an in-thread 4-element butterfly (low 2 bits of the element index) followed by a 32-lane warp-shuffle butterfly (high 5 bits), which together realize the standard Sylvester Hadamard H128[i][j]=(-1)^popcount(i&j); all arithmetic is FP32 regardless of I/O dtype, with the r_scale = scale*0.088388347648f (= scale/√128) folded into the single conversion back. Template flags pre_scale/post_scale select elementwise multiplication by an fp16 scale vector (suh sign vector) BEFORE the transform, or (svh) AFTER it; a host launch uses at most one of the two (pre XOR post — the ATen wrapper dispatches <true,false>, <false,true>, or <false,false>). Standalone kernels exist for fp16 and fp32 vectors only (scales always fp16, no bf16 anywhere); each block is one warp handling one 128-segment, grid = (rows, cols/128), and cols must be divisible by 128 — there is no partial-block path. Crucially, the same inner device functions are already fused into both the cooperative GEMM kernel (input rotation into an A_had scratch before grid.sync, output rotation in the epilogue from fp32 shmem tiles) and the GEMV kernel (which requires suh/A_had/svh unconditionally), so a port that uses those fused kernels needs the standalone rotation mainly as a BF16 adapter and for the unfused/reconstruct fallback. hadamard.cpp (Paley constructions) is quant-time-only and irrelevant to serving.

Launch: blockDim=(32) — exactly one warp; gridDim=(rows, cols/128); smem 0. Each block offsets both pointers by `(size_t)gridDim.y*128*blockIdx.x + blockIdx.y*128` (row-major, row stride = gridDim.y*128 = cols) and calls had_hf_r_128_inner. Instantiations used by the host wrapper: <true,false> (pre=suh), <false,true> (post=svh), <false,false>. r_scale passed as scale*0.088388347648f (scale/sqrt(128)). Works in place (output_ptr==input_ptr is safe: each warp fully register-resident per segment).

NOTE the inner indexes scale with blockIdx.y — the scale tensor is addressed as a full-width (cols-long) vector from its base pointer; when reusing the inner in a 1-D grid (as the GEMM does) you must pre-offset the pointer: `suh + (this_warp*128) % size_k`.

read:hadamard.dtype_notes: Standalone kernels exist for fp16 vectors (had_hf_*) and fp32 vectors (had_ff_*) only; there is NO bf16 variant anywhere in upstream (no had_bf_r_128 exists). Scale vectors (suh/svh) are ALWAYS fp16 — they are ±1 sign vectors (unpack_bf maps bits to ±1.0 half), exactly representable. Internally every variant computes the entire butterfly in FP32 (half inputs are widened immediately; shuffles move fp32 bit patterns), so numeric behavior is dtype-of-transport, not dtype-of-math; the only rounding is the single __floats2half2_rn at output (with r_scale folded in). had_fh is the one mixed pair (fp32 in, fp16 out) and exists only as a device inner for the GEMM epilogue. Upstream runs the whole EXL3 linear in fp16: exl3_gemm checks TORCH_CHECK_DTYPE(A, kHalf), C may be fp16 or fp32 (c_fp32 flag), and LinearEXL3.default_out_dtype = torch.half — a bf16 model would be down-converted by the framework before reaching these kernels; there is no bf16 path to imitate. For Atlas (BF16 activations, sometimes FP32 residual): either (a) add a bf16-in/fp16-out inner — mechanical, since the math is already fp32: replace the half4 load with bfloat164 load + __bfloat162float, keep fp16 store so the packed GEMM (which consumes fp16 A) is fed directly; this fuses the BF16→FP16 conversion into the mandatory input rotation for free (bf16→fp32→fp16 loses only range above 65504/below fp16 denormals, and the 1/√128 scaling inside the transform pulls magnitudes down before conversion); or (b) convert BF16→FP16 first and use the kernels as-is. For FP32 residual inputs the ff variant works unmodified.
read:hadamard.blackwell_notes: Nothing in the rotation machinery is architecture-gated: it is pure warp-shuffle (__shfl_xor_sync), half2 intrinsics, and atomicAdd(float*) — all sm_70-era; compiles and runs unchanged on sm_121a. __launch_bounds__(32) single-warp blocks are legal though occupancy-poor per block; the kernels are launch-bound/memory-bound and this is how upstream ships it (no need to change for GB10, but packing 4-8 warps per block is a safe optimization since segments are independent — just keep the blockIdx.y-based scale indexing or pre-offset pointers). Zero static shared memory in the standalone kernels; only had_hf_r_128_d_inner needs dynamic smem (128 floats × warps-per-block) — irrelevant to carveout limits. The one Blackwell-relevant coupling is downstream: the fused input rotation inside exl3_gemm_kernel sits before a cg::this_grid().sync(), so that path requires cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel (and the kernel-attribute/SMEM_MAX setup in exl3_gemm.cu); the standalone had kernels themselves are plain launches and CUDA-graph-safe. No sm90+ features (no TMA, no clusters, no wgmma) anywhere in this file set.
read:hadamard.port_plan: Copy verbatim: hadamard_inner.cuh minus the ACT_* section if the guad inner is deferred (the four shuffle_had_* helpers plus had_hf/ff/fh_r_128_inner are freestanding), and the half4 typedef from util.cuh; keep the inner signatures byte-identical because exl3_gemm_kernel.cuh, exl3_gemm_inner.cuh and exl3_gemv_kernel.cuh call them directly with hardcoded 0.088388347648f. Replace: the ATen host wrappers in hadamard_q.cu with a single extern-C entry, e.g. extern \"C\" int exl3_had_r_128(const void* x, void* y, const void* scale, int rows, int cols, int dtype /*0=f16,1=f32,2=bf16-in*/, int scale_mode /*0=none,1=pre,2=post*/, float scale, cudaStream_t stream) that validates cols%128==0, computes r_scale=scale*0.088388347648f, and launches grid(rows, cols/128), block(32) — the 3×template dispatch (<true,false>/<false,true>/<false,false>) collapses the optional-tensor logic; no allocations occur in this subsystem at all (A_had scratch is the GEMM's problem — Atlas should carve it from BufferArena, noting \"A_had may be reference to A\" permits in-place when A is scratch already). Add one new kernel: had_bf16_to_hf_r_128 (bf16 load → fp32 math → fp16 store, pre_scale=suh) as Atlas's activation-ingress adapter. What you actually NEED given the fusion findings: for the packed GEMM path (m>reconstruct threshold) and the GEMV path — NOTHING standalone, because both kernels fuse the input rotation (had_hf_r_128_inner<true,false> over m*k/128 warps into A_had, then grid.sync) and the output rotation (epilogue had_ff/fh_r_128_inner<false,true> from fp32 shmem tiles; GEMV hard-requires suh_ptr && A_had_ptr && svh_ptr). The standalone entry is needed only as (1) the BF16→FP16 ingress conversion point if you fuse conversion+rotation and then call the GEMM WITHOUT suh (pass suh=null so the kernel skips its pre-pass — note upstream's `// if (suh)` is commented out, so a port must restore that guard or always pass suh), (2) the unfused reconstruct-hgemm fallback for very large m (rotate input with pre=suh, hgemm against reconstructed W_hat, rotate output in-place with post=svh), and (3) parity harnesses. Recommended minimal extern-C surface: exl3_had_r_128 (dtype+mode dispatched) and exl3_had_r_128_bf16_ingress; skip dual/guad/atomic-d variants initially. Semantics to preserve exactly: pre-scale multiplies BEFORE the transform (input side, suh), post-scale AFTER transform and r_scale (output side, svh); one scale per launch, never both; H128 is Sylvester (-1)^popcount(i&j) over element index e=4*lane+j; in-place is safe. Validate against upstream with scale=1.0: y = (x.view(-1,128) @ H128/sqrt(128)).view_as(x), involutive up to sign vectors (applying twice with matching pre/post recovers x exactly in fp32).
risks: BF16→FP16 conversion at the rotation boundary: bf16 activations with |v|>65504 overflow fp16 at load if converted before the transform; converting inside the fp32 pipeline (bf16→fp32 load, fp16 store after the 1/√128 scaling) is safer but still stores fp16 — outlier activations could saturate. Mitigate by parity-checking against an fp32 reference on real Atlas activations.

Scale indexing uses blockIdx.y inside the inner (scale half4 index = blockIdx.y*32 + t): calling the inner from any kernel with a different grid shape without pre-offsetting the scale pointer (as the GEMM does with `suh + (this_warp*128) % size_k`) silently reads wrong signs — wrong answers, no crash.

The `if (suh)` guard in exl3_gemm_kernel.cuh:14 is commented out — the fused input-rotation pre-pass runs unconditionally and dereferences suh/A_had; a port that passes null suh (e.g. after a standalone ingress rotation) crashes or corrupts unless the guard is restored.

cols%128==0 is a hard requirement with no partial-block path; EXL3 checkpoints guarantee it (both sides had-transformed at quant time) but any Atlas layer with a non-128-multiple hidden slice (TP shards, head-group slices) must be rejected at load, not launch.

In-place output rotation (y==x) relies on each warp reading its full 128-segment into registers before writing; safe as written, but any restructuring to multi-warp-per-segment or vectorization changes breaks this silently.
Contiguity: upstream asserts x.is_contiguous() at the Python layer because strided views are 'silently misread as interleaved garbage'; Atlas must enforce row-contiguity at the Rust call site.

The dual/guad/atomic-d inners are consumed by MLP-fusion kernels not in this snapshot; if Atlas later ports those fused MLP kernels, the guad activation-limit clamp asymmetry (u clamped to ±limit, gate output only min'd to +limit) and the RELU2_NOGATE g-buffer-unused convention must be carried over exactly.
fp16 half2 SiLU in the guad inner (h2exp/h2rcp) is lower precision than Atlas's usual fp32 activation math — a fused-MLP port would inherit a small numeric delta vs Atlas's unfused baseline.

read:python-contract.summary: This subsystem is the runtime glue that composes EXL3 trellis-quantized linears in ExLlamaV3. Per linear it holds: trellis int16 (in/16, out/16, 16*K), unpacked sign vectors suh (in_features,) fp16 and svh (out_features,) fp16, optional fp16 bias, and CPU-resident presence-flag tensors mcg/mul1 that select the procedural-codebook variant (cb = 0 plain / 1 mcg / 2 mul1; K derived as trellis.shape[-1]//16). Forward has exactly two regimes gated on total rows M = numel/last_dim: for M <= AUTO_RECONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD = 144 it runs the quantized kernels via a prebuilt C++ bound context (`self.bc.run_alloc(x, out_features, dtype==torch.float)`, BC_LinearEXL3 wrapping exl3_gemm_gr which internally applies suh+Hadamard into an A_had scratch, does the trellis matmul, and applies Hadamard+svh on the output — a QTIP-style GEMV sub-path fires inside exl3_gemm for m <= 8); for M > 144 it dequantizes the whole weight to fp16 (`reconstruct`/`reconstruct_had_slice`, sliced at 32768 output columns) and runs a plain fp16 `hgemm`, with explicit `had_r_128` input/output rotations unless the fused reconstruct variant (rows >= 1024, dims % 128 == 0) folds both Hadamards and both sign vectors into the reconstruct kernel so the gemm runs in the original basis. Batched/fused compositions (gate+up, MoE experts) go through `ext.exl3_mgemm`, which takes int64 device-pointer tables for trellis/suh/svh plus optional per-token expert `indices` and fp16 `weights` (weighted reduction into C[0]) and min/max_index expert-range filtering for EP shards. Everything is fp16-centric: A must be fp16 contiguous, C is fp16 or fp32, and there is no bf16 anywhere in the path.

symbols.name: LinearEXL3.forward
symbols.contract: forward(x, params, out_dtype) -> Tensor. Requires x fp16 CONTIGUOUS (`assert x.is_contiguous()`); rows = x.numel() // x.shape[-1]. Path A (rows <= 144 or infer_params.no_reconstruct): `return self.bc.run_alloc(x, self.out_features, dtype == torch.float)` where dtype = out_dtype or self.default_out_dtype (default torch.half) — the bool selects fp32 C. Path B (rows > 144): reconstruct_hgemm(x, out_dtype). Bias is applied inside bc on path A; python adds `y += self.bias` on path B.
symbols.notes: AUTO_RECONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD = 144, MAX_RECONSTRUCT_SLICE_N = 32768, RECONSTRUCT_SLICE_GRANULARITY_N = 128. bc built at __init__: `ext.BC_LinearEXL3(trellis, suh, svh, K, bias, mcg: bool, mul1: bool, g_tensor_cache.get(device, (1, in_features), out_dtype))` — last arg is a cached bsz-1 xh (A_had) scratch. mcg/mul1 tensors themselves live on CPU and are only presence flags.

symbols.name: exl3_gemm
symbols.contract: int exl3_gemm(const at::Tensor& A, const at::Tensor& B, at::Tensor& C, optional suh, optional A_had, optional svh, int force_shape_idx, bool mcg, bool mul1, int force_num_sms). A: row-major fp16 (m,k) contiguous (m folded over leading dims); B: int16 trellis (k/16, n/16, 16*K), K = B.size(2)/16; C: fp16 or fp32 (m,n), need not be zeroed; suh fp16 (k,), svh fp16 (n,); A_had fp16 scratch same size as A (required with suh; may alias A). Constraints k % 16 == 0, n % 128 == 0. cb = mcg?1 : mul1?2 : 0; TORCH_CHECK !(mcg&&mul1). Kernel args array (10 ptrs, fixed order): {A_ptr, B_ptr, C_ptr, size_m, size_k, size_n, locks, suh_ptr, A_had_ptr, svh_ptr}. Dispatch order: (1) int8-activation GEMV if mul1 && EXL3_INT8_GEMV=1; (2) QTIP GEMV via exl3_gemv_try_launch (only if suh && A_had && svh and force_shape_idx<=0 && force_num_sms<=0); (3) cooperative autotune over shape_idx 1..EXL3_GEMM_NUM_SHAPES=4, launched with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel(kernel, num_sms, block_dim, args, SMEM_MAX, stream) after cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, SMEM_MAX). Shape tables: TILESIZE_K {-,16,32,32,16}, TILESIZE_N {-,128,128,256,512}, BLOCKDIM {-,256,512,512,256} (index 0 unused). Autotune hash mixes min(roundup_pow2(m),16), k, n, K, c_fp32, device, cc, num_sms, cb. Returns shape_idx (90 for gemv path).
symbols.notes: suh/svh application is INSIDE the kernel on this path: kernel writes Hadamard(x*suh)/sqrt(128) into A_had, then trellis matmul, then Hadamard+*svh on output. Python never calls had_r_128 on this path.

symbols.name: exl3_gemv (+ exl3_gemv_try_launch heuristic)
symbols.contract: void exl3_gemv(A, B, C, suh, A_had, svh, bool mcg, bool mul1) — forced entry; normally reached via exl3_gemv_try_launch(kernel_args, m, k, n, K, cb, c_fp32, has_su_sv, device, stream, &kernel, force) from inside exl3_gemm. Hard eligibility: suh+A_had+svh all present, 2 <= K <= 4, (K==4 || cb!=0), m <= EXL3_GEMV_MAX_M = 8, k % 128 == 0, n % 128 == 0. Env EXL3_GEMV: 0 off, 1/unset heuristic, 2 wherever legal. Kernel template exl3_gemv_kernel<bits, c_fp32, cb, mmode(m==1?0:1), cfg(0 narrow/1 wide), smem>. Narrow cfg: block 512, one block per 32 output cols; wide: block 256, 64 cols. grid = min(n/cols, occupancy-capped max), cooperative launch, 0 dynamic smem. Same 10-arg kernel array as exl3_gemm.
symbols.notes: Heuristic comment: measured wins on Ampere/Ada; 'Ada/Blackwell are memory-bound here and keep the regular kernel' — but the cc gate is commented out, so on GB10 the path still fires when the shape branch matches (K==2 always for n<=8192; narrow when n/32 <= co-resident blocks or k<=2048&&n<=8192; wide for n>=8192&&k<=4096; K==3 non-Ada otherwise declines).

symbols.name: exl3_mgemm
symbols.contract: int exl3_mgemm(A, B, C, suh, A_had, svh, optional indices, optional weights, int K, int force_shape_idx, uint32 mcg_mult, uint32 mul1_mult, int min_index, int max_index, int force_num_sms, int num_tokens = 1, optional size_n_list, optional c_ptrs). A: fp16 (a_batches, m, k) contiguous; C: fp16/fp32 (c_batches, m, n); B/suh/svh: int64 1-D DEVICE-POINTER TABLES (one address per quantized matrix; entry q: trellis (k/16,n/16,16K) u16, suh (k,) f16, svh (n,) f16 — the C doc comment says 'logically (k/16)'/'(n/16)' for suh/svh but python passes full unpacked fp16 vectors); A_had fp16 scratch, MUST hold bszm*m*k elements (bszm = max(bszm_in, bszm_out)) — 'an undersized scratch is silent OOB corruption'. indices: int64 (*, num_indices), slot j uses q = indices[j], negative skips; weights: fp16 parallel to indices -> each result scaled by weights[j] and ALL active C[j] summed into C[0] (C doubles as per-expert scratch). a_batches == 1 broadcasts A[0], transformed separately per selected B[q] (per-matrix suh). min_index >= 0 enables expert-range filtering [min_index, max_index) with index rebasing (EP shard-local pointer tables); num_tokens==1 compacts retained indices, num_tokens>1 masks out-of-range slots to -1 in place preserving per-token slot groups; max 128 slots. size_n_list (int32) + c_ptrs (int64) enable per-matrix output widths (requires num_tokens==1, no filtering, no weights). Grid: dim3(num_sms, 1, concurrency = min(total_sms/num_sms, bszm)), cooperative, SMEM_MAX. 19-entry kernel-args array appends {indices_ptr, weights_ptr, bszm_in, bszm_out, min_index, max_index, num_tokens, size_n_list_ptr, c_list_ptr} to the 10 gemm args.
symbols.notes: Exact python call from GatedMLP fused gate+up (bsz*q_len <= 32, non-graphed path): `ext.exl3_mgemm(x.view(1, m, dim), mgu.ptrs_trellis, gu, mgu.ptrs_suh, guh, mgu.ptrs_svh, None, None, mgu.K, -1, mgu.mcg, mgu.mul1, -1, -1, 0, 1, None, None)` with gu = empty (2, m, out_f) interm_dtype, guh = empty (2, m, dim) interm_dtype (the A_had scratch: bszm=2 slabs). Then g=gu[0], u=gu[1], fused activation, down.forward(a).

symbols.name: had_r_128
symbols.contract: void had_r_128(input, output, optional pre_scale, optional post_scale, float scale). input/output 2-D, same shape/dtype (fp16 or fp32), cols % 128 == 0; in-place OK (output may alias input). Computes y = (x.view(-1,128) @ H128).view(shape) * scale/sqrt(128); r_scale = scale * 0.088388347648f. pre_scale: elementwise fp16 multiply BEFORE the transform (input side: x*suh then H); post_scale: AFTER (output side: H(y) then *svh). At most one of the two per call (dual variant had_r_128_dual does two tensors in one launch). Grid dim3(rows, cols/128), block dim3(32), 0 smem. Kernels: had_hf_r_128_kernel<pre,post> (fp16), had_ff_r_128_kernel (fp32), __launch_bounds__(32).
symbols.notes: Python calls (unfused reconstruct path only): input `ext.had_r_128(x, xh, self.suh, None, 1.0)`; output IN-PLACE `ext.had_r_128(y_, y_, None, self.svh, 1.0)`. Matches W = diag(suh)·H128·W_hat·H128·diag(svh).

symbols.name: LinearEXL3.reconstruct_hgemm
symbols.contract: Large-M path (rows > 144). use_fused = (in%128==0 and out%128==0, always true for EXL3) and rows >= 1024 and not EXL3_NO_FUSED_RECONSTRUCT. Unfused: xh = empty_like(x); had_r_128(x, xh, suh, None, 1.0); then per output slice of MAX_RECONSTRUCT_SLICE_N=32768 cols: w = empty (in_features, slice_n) fp16; ext.reconstruct(w, trellis, K, mcg, mul1) or ext.reconstruct_slice(w, trellis, K, mcg, mul1, n_start); ext.hgemm(xh, w, y_slice); finally had_r_128(y_, y_, None, svh, 1.0) in place; bias added in python. Fused (rows >= 1024): xh = x (raw input, no had launches); ext.reconstruct_had_slice(w, trellis, suh, svh_sliced (= svh[n_start:]), K, mcg, mul1, n_start) emits ORIGINAL-basis weights (both Hadamards + both sign vectors folded in); hgemm on raw x; no output had. Fused reconstruct costs ~4x plain (k*n-bound) vs saved had launches scaling rows*(k+n); breakeven rows ~400-900, gate set at 1024.
symbols.notes: y allocated as out_shape (..., out_features) in out_dtype or default (half); hgemm writes fp16 or fp32 per C dtype. This path is ~the whole prefill regime for Atlas.

symbols.name: BC_LinearEXL3
symbols.contract: ext.BC_LinearEXL3(trellis, suh, svh, K: int, bias, mcg: bool, mul1: bool, xh_cached) — C++ bound context prebuilt per linear (source not in ref set; libtorch/). Method used: run_alloc(x, out_features: int, c_fp32: bool) -> C tensor; wraps exl3_gemm_gr with the linear's tensors, allocating C and (for bsz 1) reusing the cached (1, in_features) xh scratch. Also the composable unit passed into BC_MLP / BC_GatedMLP graphed bsz-1/bszN paths.
symbols.notes: For the Atlas port this is just: allocate/obtain C and A_had, call the gemm dispatch — no torch needed.

symbols.name: BC_GatedMLP / BC_MLP (graphed small-batch MLP contexts)
symbols.contract: BC_GatedMLP(gu, a1, a2, down_xh, ptrs_trellis|None, ptrs_suh|None, ptrs_svh|None, K|0, mcg: bool, mul1: bool, act_silu, act_gelu, act_relu2, gate_bc|None, up_bc|None, down_bc, act_limit) with cached statics gu (2, MAX_BSZN, hidden_size) interm_dtype, a1 (2, MAX_BSZN, out_f) interm_dtype, a2 (1, MAX_BSZN, out_f) half, down_xh (1, MAX_BSZN, out_f) half; method run_bszN(x_view(1, bsz*q_len, dim), d_view) used when bsz*q_len <= MAX_BSZN = 8, internally CUDA-graph-replayed from 3rd call. BC_MLP(xp, u, ones, yp, act flags, up_bc, down_bc, act_limit, hidden_size, out_size); run_bsz1(x, d) for bsz==1 && q_len==1 && fp16 && contiguous. Eligibility for the fused gate+up mgemm arm: both exl3, same out_features and K, no biases, and infer_params.use_mgemm(K, out_features, mul1_both, device).
symbols.notes: MAX_BSZN = 8 'must match MAX_BSZN in exllamav3_ext/libtorch/mlp.h'. Activation fns for gated path: ext.silu_mul / gelu_mul / relu2_mul(g, u, a, act_limit) writing fp16 a; if interm_dtype == torch.float the activation output is still fp16 (fresh half tensor).

symbols.name: MultiLinear (pointer-table aggregate)
symbols.contract: MultiLinear(device, [linears]) — builds the int64 device-pointer tables consumed by exl3_mgemm: ptrs_trellis, ptrs_suh, ptrs_svh (one entry per member linear), plus scalars K (shared), out_features, mcg, mul1 (shared flags). Used for fused gate+up ([gate, up] -> bszm 2) and, in the (absent-from-ref) block_sparse_mlp.py, for per-expert tables driven by indices/weights.
symbols.notes: Module source not in the ref set; contract inferred from construction/usage in py_mlp.py and the exl3_mgemm checks (B/suh/svh int64 1-D, equal length).

symbols.name: DevCtx (locks + workspace singleton)
symbols.contract: Per-device lazily-allocated state the kernels require: get_locks(device) -> int* of (MAX_TILES_C + MAX_BARRIERS*2 + MOE_SCHED_INTS) ints, cudaMemset 0 at creation, with MAX_TILES_C = 1024*1024, MAX_BARRIERS = 1024, BARRIER_LOCKS_OFFSET = MAX_TILES_C, MOE_SCHED_OFFSET = MAX_TILES_C + 2*MAX_BARRIERS, MOE_SCHED_INTS = 2 + MOE_MAX_GROUPS (MOE_MAX_GROUPS defined elsewhere); passed as the 7th kernel arg to every gemm/gemv/mgemm launch (cooperative-grid tile locks/barriers; must be zeroed and persistent). get_ws(device): 16 MiB scratch (WORKSPACE_SIZE). get_num_sms / get_cc: cc mapping major>=10 -> CC_BLACKWELL=5, >=9 HOPPER=4, 8.9 ADA=3, >=8 AMPERE=2 else CC_OLD=1.
symbols.notes: Atlas must reproduce this: a ~4.01 MB zero-initialized int lock buffer per device, shared by all EXL3 launches on that device (safe because launches on one stream serialize).

symbols.name: exl3_gemm shape/autotune tables
symbols.contract: EXL3_GEMM_NUM_SHAPES = 4; per shape_idx 1..4: TILESIZE_K {16,32,32,16}, TILESIZE_N {128,128,256,512}, BLOCKDIM {256,512,512,256}. num_sms for a candidate = max(min(size_k/tk * size_n/tn, device_sms), 1). Non-autotuned mgemm sizing: num_sms = tiles, clamp num_sms*bszm <= total_sms (num_sms = max(total_sms/bszm,1)), double num_sms if tiles/num_sms > 48, concurrency = min(total_sms/num_sms, bszm), grid = (num_sms, 1, concurrency).
symbols.notes: Runtime CoopKernelAutotuner (coop_autotune.cuh, not in ref set) times candidates keyed by mgemm_autotune_hash which additionally mixes min(bszm_in,24), min(bszm_out,24). A port can replace it with a static per-shape pick for GB10 measured offline; force_shape_idx + force_num_sms already bypass it.

symbols.name: AUTO_RECONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD / gemv threshold constants
symbols.contract: AUTO_RECONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD = 144 (python: rows <= 144 -> quantized kernels, else dequant+hgemm); EXL3_GEMV_MAX_M = 8 (exl3_gemv_kernel.cuh; gemv kernels have MMODE 0 for m==1, MMODE 1 for 2..8 with constexpr ROWS = 8); fused-reconstruct gate rows >= 1024; mgemm python arm gate bsz*q_len <= 32; graphed bszN gate bsz*q_len <= MAX_BSZN = 8.
symbols.notes: These four numbers define the entire regime ladder: 1 / <=8 / <=32(gated-mlp mgemm) / <=144 / >144 / >=1024.

read:python-contract.dtype_notes: The entire quantized path is fp16-in: A must be torch.half contiguous (TORCH_CHECK_DTYPE(A, kHalf) in gemm/gemv/mgemm) and python asserts contiguity but never casts — there is NO bf16 handling anywhere in exl3.py/linear.py/mlp.py; bf16 tensors would fail the dtype check. C (output) is fp16 by default or fp32 when out_dtype == torch.float (c_fp32 template flag; run_alloc's third arg) — this is the hook Atlas should use for its FP32 residual highway. suh/svh are always fp16 (unpacked from int16 bitfields at load if needed: bit b -> 1.0 - 2.0*b, i.e. {+1,-1} fp16), full length in_features/out_features. trellis is int16 viewed as uint16. bias fp16 (fp32 checkpoint bias cast to half at load). had_r_128 supports fp16 AND fp32 tensors (hf/ff kernel pairs) but the scale vectors are always fp16. mcg/mul1 are CPU tensors used only as booleans (the C ext takes uint32_t mcg_mult/mul1_mult but only truthiness reaches the kernel selector: cb = mcg?1: mul1?2 :0). Reconstructed w is fp16 (in_features, out_features); hgemm is fp16 x fp16 -> fp16 or fp32. interm_dtype == torch.float in MLPs only changes the up/gate output buffer; the fused activation always writes a fresh fp16 tensor before the down projection. Accumulation inside the trellis kernels is not visible at this layer (see kernel files); the mgemm weighted-MoE reduction accumulates expert outputs into C[0] in C's dtype — fp32 C is available and preferable for many-expert sums. For Atlas/BF16: convert activations bf16->fp16 before A (or extend the had+quantize input stage to read bf16), and either take fp16 C or fp32 C then cast to bf16.
read:python-contract.blackwell_notes: DevCtx maps prop.major >= 10 to CC_BLACKWELL = 5 — note GB10/sm_121a reports major 12, so it lands in CC_BLACKWELL correctly via the >= 10 catch-all. cc only feeds heuristics, not correctness: exl3_gemv_cfg has Ampere/Ada-specific branches (K==3 wide only on CC_ADA; one wide-band shape only on CC_AMPERE) and its source comments say Ada/Blackwell are memory-bound and prefer the regular kernel, yet the `if (cc != CC_AMPERE) return -1` gate is COMMENTED OUT, so on GB10 the QTIP gemv still fires for K==2 (any n<=8192 narrow / >8192 wide), and for other K via the co-residency/small-k branches — a port should re-measure this envelope on sm_121a rather than trust it. All three matmul entry points use cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel with grid-wide sync plus a persistent zeroed locks buffer; sm_121a supports cooperative launch, but grid size must respect co-residency (the code caps grids via cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor and per-shape max_slices). Every gemm/mgemm kernel needs cudaFuncSetAttribute(cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, SMEM_MAX) before first launch (SMEM_MAX defined in the kernel headers; GB10's 99KB/block dynamic-smem class must satisfy it — verify against exl3_gemm_kernel.cuh's SMEM_MAX when porting). The runtime autotuner benches all 4 shape indices per (m-class, k, n, K, cb, fp32, device) on first use; on a single fixed target (GB10 only) Atlas can pre-bake the winners and call the select_* static path (force_shape_idx) instead. Nothing in the host code is sm90+/TMA-specific — plain cp.async-era kernels — so sm_121a compilation is a straight -arch matter for the kernel headers.

Mirror the Python regime ladder in Rust: M<=144 quantized path (with gemv sub-heuristic re-measured on GB10, EXL3_GEMV_MAX_M=8, K in 2..4, k%128==0 && n%128==0), M>144 reconstruct+gemm sliced at 32768 output cols with fp16 w scratch (in_features * min(n,32768) * 2 bytes), fused-reconstruct variant at M>=1024 (skips all 4 had launches). BF16 seam: add a tiny bf16->fp16 cast kernel in front of A (and fp32-C out then cast to bf16), or template the input-transform stage on the activation type — the had inner already has an fp32 instantiation to crib from. Per-linear device tensors to load from EXL3 checkpoints: trellis int16 (k/16, n/16, 16K), suh f16 (k,), svh f16 (n,), optional bias f16, mcg/mul1 presence -> cb constant; K = last_dim/16; enforce k%16==0, n%128==0 (EXL3 quant pads to 128 already).

read:atlas-surface.summary: Atlas today treats EXL3 as a load-time format only: `serve_load.rs`/`factory/build.rs` call `materialize_exl3()` immediately after the store loads, which reconstructs every `{p}.trellis/.suh/.svh[/.mul1]` linear to BF16 on-GPU (via the already-ported `exl3_reconstruct.cu` kernels), re-quantizes expert-family prefixes to ModelOpt-style NVFP4 triplets, writes plain BF16 `.weight` for everything else, and frees the packed tensors — so nothing EXL3 survives into serving. Native serving means keeping `Exl3Weight` (trellis/suh/svh DevicePtrs + in_dim/out_dim/k_bits/cb, resolved by `Exl3Weight::from_store`) resident and adding a dispatch arm beside the existing Nvfp4/Fp8/Dense/PackedQ2 arms of the unified `QuantWeight` enum, plus a `WeightQuantFormat::Exl3` tag so the MoE `experts_scale_kind` machinery (the E8M0 precedent) can later route a grouped-GEMM exl3 arm. The MoE grouped path has a crisp, stable contract (token-major BF16 A + per-expert u64 pointer tables + `expert_offsets` prefix sums + `sorted_token_ids` gather + sorted-layout BF16 C) that an exl3 mgemm can mirror by swapping the three NVFP4 tables (packed/scale/scale2) for three EXL3 tables (trellis/suh/svh) plus uniform K/cb scalars. Activations at every linear call site are BF16 `[m,K]` in / BF16 `[m,N]` out (the qwen4_exp FP32 "highway" is only the residual stream; linears read post-norm BF16), so fp16-only vendored kernels need a bf16→fp16 hop that is best fused into the mandatory input-side Hadamard/suh rotation stage, and an fp16→bf16 (svh-scaled) epilogue. Build-wise, only top-level `.cu` files in `kernels/gb10/common/` become modules (module name = file stem, overridable in KERNEL.toml `[modules]`); vendored `.cuh` headers go in a subdirectory (`common/exl3_vendor/`), which is the exact `q4k_vendor` precedent — headers are include-only, tracked by the directory-level `cargo:rerun-if-changed` on the common dir and hashed by the include-closure attestation (unresolved includes emit build warnings).

The qwen4_exp "FP32 highway" is the RESIDUAL stream only — linears consume post-norm BF16, so an fp16-only EXL3 GEMM never sees FP32 input directly. Weights: EXL3 aux vectors suh/svh are EXACT f16 bits and the loader already exempts them from the default F16→BF16 conversion (is_exl3_f16_aux); trellis is u16 codes; decode math is fp16 with precisely-ordered __hadd/__hfma/__hmul (bit-parity CPU oracle exists in exl3.rs cpu_ref). Where the bf16→fp16 hop goes if vendored kernels are fp16-only: the EXL3 mm requires an input-side rotation anyway (x ← (x ⊙ suh) · H128 per 128-block, upstream materializes A_had fp16), so the cheapest correct placement is to FUSE the bf16 load into that rotation kernel (read bf16, convert to fp16/f32 in-register, rotate, store A_had fp16) — no standalone conversion pass and no extra memory traffic; Atlas has no bf16→f16 utility kernel today (only bf16_to_fp8), so one would otherwise have to be added. Output side: upstream applies svh in the epilogue; the vendored store should be modified (or wrapped) to emit BF16 directly (f16 accum → f32 → __float2bfloat16, one rounding — exl3_f16_to_bf16_t shows the exact convention), otherwise a second elementwise fp16→bf16 pass per call is needed. For a future grouped-MoE arm the same holds: A gather (sorted_token_ids) + suh + H128 + bf16→fp16 fuse into one prologue; C must land sorted-layout BF16 so silu_mul/down/unpermute stay byte-identical.
read:atlas-surface.blackwell_notes: Atlas builds ONE arch per hardware dir: kernels/gb10/HARDWARE.toml `arch` (sm_121a) is applied to every .cu by nvcc (CUDA 13); there are no per-arch #if branches in the Atlas-side files read here, and nothing sm90+-only in the reconstruct kernel (dp4a, shf.r.wrap, bfe, lop3, __shfl_*_sync all fine on sm_121a). Grid conventions are tuned for GB10's small SM count (comments cite 48 SMs / 128-wide N tiles / persistent 96-CTA grids); the fused MoE kernels use grid.z = num_experts with early-exit or compacted worklists — an exl3 grouped kernel should follow the (n_tiles, max_m_tiles, num_experts) shape or the worklist pattern. Shared-memory ceiling is the practical constraint: the GpuBackend trait exposes NO cuFuncSetAttribute, so >48KB dynamic smem is unreachable without extending spark-runtime; exl3_reconstruct.cu stays static-__shared__ (~40KB worst case at K=8) and any vendored exl3_gemm must be trimmed to ≤48KB static or the trait must grow a max-dynamic-smem setter. Decode-graph capture exists on this target (ctx.graph_capture disables the exact-tiles D2H sync path) — any new launch path must avoid host-blocking D2H under capture, and pageable H2D / swallowed-error syncs are known graph poisons on qwen4_exp. TMA is available through arg_tensormap if a future kernel wants it, but no existing MoE kernel here uses it.

quant_gemv/quant_gemm signatures carry exactly 3 KernelHandles; an Exl3 arm either resolves handles internally (per-call registry lookup — against convention on hot paths) or every caller signature widens (large diff). The PackedQ2 precedent (bail + layer-site dispatch) sidesteps this for milestone 1 but scatters dispatch.

Per-call A_had scratch + bf16→fp16 conversion allocates on the hot path; decode-graph capture forbids host-blocking allocs/syncs mid-capture (901 playbook) — scratch must come from the BufferArena or be pre-sized at construction, and no D2H sync may be added under ctx.graph_capture.

materialize_exl3 keep-resident mode must keep memory accounting honest: leaving experts packed while also building NVFP4 triplets (transition period) would double-count; and suh/svh exact-f16 exemption must survive any new load path (silent BF16 conversion = wrong weights).

Native EXL3 experts under EP: EP name filtering already parses .trellis/.suh/.svh/.mul1 expert indices (tested), but the grouped kernel must skip NULL trellis pointers AND any worklist builder must test them (the #781 class of bug).

The startup kernel audit fails closed on unresolved lookups: new gpu.kernel()/try_kernel names must ship in every target that dispatches them or be declared [expected_absent] in MODEL.toml — a new module compiled only into some targets will otherwise block startup on the rest.

K/cb uniformity across MoE experts is assumed by a single-launch grouped kernel; EXL3 quantizes per-tensor, so a checkpoint could mix K per expert — assert at table build, or the kernel needs per-expert K (heavier).
