fp16 accumulation semantics of the vendored GEMM differ from Atlas's f32-accum BF16 kernels; A/B against the materialized-NVFP4 baseline AND a BF16-reconstruct reference before claiming fidelity wins (the double-quant argument cuts both ways at small K).

read:parity-bench-design.summary: This subsystem is ExLlamaV3's native EXL3 trellis matmul: activations are rotated per-128-block (x -> diag(suh)·H128·x·(1/sqrt(128)), fp32 math, one fp16 rounding at store into A_had scratch), multiplied against the packed 16x16-tile trellis stream decoded on the fly to m16n8k16 B-fragments, then output-rotated (H128·y·(1/sqrt(128))·diag(svh)). Three kernels cover it: exl3_gemv_kernel (m<=8, warps split k, B streamed to registers with __ldcs, fp16 MMA accumulation folded to fp32 every FOLD slices, cross-warp fp32 smem reduction), exl3_gemm_kernel (m<=16 per pass, cp.async 3-stage pipeline, fp32 MMA accumulation on every arch except sm_86, cross-BLOCK k-slice reduction through global memory guarded by a lock array), and exl3_mgemm_kernel (pointer-table batched/MoE variant with expert-range filtering, per-expert weights, and a grouped final reduction). The verification design below gives (a) derived tolerance gates for the inexact end-to-end oracle vs a CPU f64 truth pipeline, calibrated against the bf16-materialized path, (b) two bit-exact sub-oracles (tile decode, and the 128-point rotation whose kernel math is pure fp32 with a single terminal rounding), (c) a qwen4_exp-shaped bench matrix vs the shipping NVFP4 kernels with a concrete win criterion, and (d) an example-binary layout that follows exl3_reconstruct_parity's leg/control/exit-code conventions.

symbols.name: exl3_gemv_kernel
symbols.contract: template <int bits, bool c_fp32, int cb, int MMODE, int CFG, bool SMEM_STAGE> __global__ __launch_bounds__(CFG==0?512:256) void exl3_gemv_kernel(EXL3_GEMM_ARGS) where EXL3_GEMM_ARGS = (const half* A, const uint16_t* B, void* C, int size_m, int size_k, int size_n, int* locks, const half* suh, half* A_had, const half* svh). bits in {2,3,4}; MMODE 0 = m==1 fast path, MMODE 1 = 2<=m<=8 (EXL3_GEMV_MAX_M=8) with row-guarded fragment loads; CFG 0 'narrow' = 512 threads, WK=16 k-split warps, WNT=2 n-tiles/warp, PF=4, FOLD=4, 32 output cols/block; CFG 1 'wide' = 256 threads, WK=8, WNT=4, PF=2, FOLD=2, 64 cols/block. Grid = min(size_n/cols, occupancy*num_SMs), COOPERATIVE launch upstream (grid.sync only brackets the input/output Hadamard stages -> removable by splitting rotation into separate launches). Static shared: float sh_red[WK][ROWS][COLS] (CFG0/MMODE1: 16*8*32*4 = 16 KB) + optional sh_stage; dynamic smem 0. Constraints: size_k%128==0, size_n%128==0, K in {2,3,4}, cb!=0 unless K==4. For sm_121a instantiate: bits in {2,3,4} x cb=2 (mul1) x c_fp32 in {false,true} x MMODE {0,1} x CFG {0,1}, SMEM_STAGE=false (shuffle extraction is the default; smem staging is a test arm).
symbols.notes: fp16 MMA accumulation by design (FragC_h), folded to fp32 on cadence: 'if ((d + 1) % FOLD == 0 || i + 1 == myn)' -> acc0 += __low2float/__high2float. This is the leg that needs the loose tolerance gate. B loads: '__ldcs(bp + (size_t)i*slice_stride + l*LSTRIDE)' with slice_stride = ntiles*TWORDS (TWORDS=8*bits u32/tile), LSTRIDE = bits==3?24:32.

symbols.name: exl3_gemm_kernel
symbols.contract: template<EXL3_GEMM_T_ARGS> __global__ __launch_bounds__(256*TILESIZE_K/16) void exl3_gemm_kernel(EXL3_GEMM_ARGS). T-args: (bits, c_fp32, cb, TILESIZE_M=16, TILESIZE_K, TILESIZE_N, SH_STAGES, FRAG_STAGES). Live shapes: SHAPE_2 = (16,32,128,4,3) blockdim 512; SHAPE_3 = (16,32,256,4,3) blockdim 512; SHAPE_4 = (16,16,512,4,3) blockdim 256. Grid = num_sms (1D), capped to slices = (size_k/TILESIZE_K)*(size_n/TILESIZE_N); dynamic smem = SMEM_MAX = 90*1024 (requires cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize opt-in). Loops m in chunks of 16 rows internally (while size_m_>0 ... A_ += 16*size_k). Requires zero-initialized locks buffer (see DevCtx layout). size_k % TILESIZE_K == 0 and size_n % TILESIZE_N == 0 are hard (tiles_k = size_k/TILESIZE_K exact); host must pick a compatible shape (all qwen4_exp shapes divide: k=2560/{16,32}, n in {640,6144,10240,248320} all %128==0, 248320/512=485).
symbols.notes: fp32 MMA accumulation on sm_121a (EXL3_GEMM_H_ACC is sm_86-only). The upstream kernel's output Hadamard is fused per-tile via shmem_out_had=true epilogue (write_sum_tile_sh + output_had_sh_gl with had_fh/ff_r_128_inner); the standalone epilogue block at the end is commented out.

symbols.name: exl3_gemm_kernel_inner
symbols.contract: template<EXL3_GEMM_T_ARGS, bool shmem_out_had> __device__ void exl3_gemm_kernel_inner(const half* A, const uint16_t* B, void* C, int size_m(<=16), int size_k, int size_n, int* locks, const half* post_scale). 3-deep cp.async pipeline (SH_STAGES), FRAG_STAGES-deep register pipeline, XOR-swizzled A smem (col ^ ((row>>SHIFT)&MASK), A_COLS=TILESIZE_K/8, SHIFT = A_COLS<=2?2:1), B dequant via dq_dispatch<bits,cb>(shb, lane_id<<3, fragB0, fragB1). Cross-block reduction: blocks covering one n-column of k-slices serialize in REVERSE slice order through barrier_acquire(lock, lock_i)/barrier_release(lock, lock_d, last) with partial sums round-tripped through global C (read_sum_gl/write_sum_gl in fp32 or fp16 depending on c_fp32) — grid MUST be fully co-resident or the spin-locks can deadlock; keep the num_sms grid cap.
symbols.notes: For c_fp32=false the inter-block partial sums are stored as fp16 ('__floats2half2_rn(frag_c...)') — an extra rounding per k-column handoff. Prefer c_fp32=true legs in the harness and in serving; convert to bf16 in the output-rotation kernel.

symbols.name: exl3_mgemm_kernel
symbols.contract: template<EXL3_GEMM_T_ARGS> __global__ void exl3_mgemm_kernel(EXL3_MGEMM_ARGS): (const half* A, const uint16_t** B_list, void* C, int size_m, int size_k, int size_n, int* locks, const half** suh_list, half* A_had, const half** svh_list, int64_t* B_indices, half* B_weights, int bszm_in, int bszm_out, int min_index, int max_index, int num_tokens, const int* size_n_list, void** C_list). Grid dim3(num_sms, 1, concurrency) where concurrency = min(total_sms/num_sms, bszm); one z-slice per active matrix iteration (for i in 0..bszm step gridDim.z). A_had scratch MUST hold bszm*m*k halfs (upstream: 'an undersized scratch is silent OOB corruption'). MAX_INDICES=128 (device-global v_indices[128]/v_weights[128] compaction). Expert-range filtering: min_index>=0 compacts (num_tokens==1) or position-preserving-masks (num_tokens>1, slots -1'd in place). Per-expert epilogue scale = 0.088388347648f * B_weights[j]. Final grouped reduction (blockIdx.z==0): each token t sums its stride = bszm/num_tokens contiguous slots into row t — in fp32 for c_fp32, in fp16 __hadd chain otherwise.
symbols.notes: On __CUDA_ARCH__ > 890 (sm_121a qualifies) the per-iteration sync is group_barrier(blockIdx.z, gridDim.x, locks + BARRIER_LOCKS_OFFSET) instead of grid.sync — the z-groups run decoupled. This is the kernel matching Atlas's grouped MoE call (10 active of 512 experts); the weights+fp16 reduction path is why the expert leg should use c_fp32.

symbols.name: had_hf_r_128_inner
symbols.contract: template <bool pre_scale, bool post_scale> __device__ void had_hf_r_128_inner(const half* in, half* out, const half* scale, float r_scale). One warp transforms one 128-vector: lane t loads half4 = elements [4t..4t+3]; optional pre-scale in fp16 (__hmul2, one rounding) BEFORE the fp32 convert; 4-point butterfly in fp32 (h0=s0+s1, h1=d0+d1, h2=s0-s1, h3=d0-d1 from s0=v0+v1,d0=v0-v1,s1=v2+v3,d1=v2-v3); then shuffle_had_f4x32: 5 XOR stages i=1,2,4,8,16 (loop '#pragma unroll for (int i = 1; i < 32; i <<= 1)') in fp32 where the lane with (lane&i)!=0 sign-flips its OWN value then adds the partner ('i0 ^= sfm & 0x80000000; h0 = __uint_as_float(i0) + ph0'); then h*r_scale in fp32 and ONE rounding via __floats2half2_rn; optional post-scale in fp16. r_scale is always the literal 0.088388347648f (1/sqrt(128)). Sister variants had_ff_r_128_inner (float in/out, uses shuffle_had_f2x32, scales applied as fp32 multiplies) and had_fh_r_128_inner (float in, half out; post-scale in fp16 after the rounding).
symbols.notes: THE bit-exact sub-oracle: every arithmetic step between load and the single terminal rounding is fp32 with a fixed order, so a CPU f32 replica (same butterfly order, same 5-stage XOR schedule, same sign-then-add orientation) reproduces it exactly. Indexing quirk: 'int i = blockIdx.y * 32 + t' means scale is indexed per 128-block via blockIdx.y in upstream's standalone had kernels; in the fused gemm/gemv use the passed scale pointer is already offset ('suh + (this_warp * 128) % size_k') and blockIdx.y==0.

symbols.name: decode_pair_cb2_dp4a_
symbols.contract: __device__ half2 decode_pair_cb2_dp4a_(uint32_t x0, uint32_t x1): x *= 0x83DCD12Du; sum = __dp4a(x, 0x01010101u, 0x6400u); result = __hfma2(halves(sum0,sum1 reinterpreted as f16 bits), k_inv=0x1eee (~1/147.7), k_bias=0xc931 (-10.39)). Bit-identical to the vabsdiff4 form and to cpu_ref::decode_code(Mul1). cb 0/1 go through decode_3inst_2<cb> (codebook.cuh): Inst3 = w*89226354+64248484, Mcg = w*0xCBAC1FED, both then (x & 0x8fff8fff) ^ 0x3b603b60 and __hadd of the two f16 halves.
symbols.notes: Already covered bit-exactly by cpu_ref::decode_code + the shipped exl3_reconstruct_parity gate; the matmul port reuses the identical device code.

symbols.name: dq8_regs_4bits / dq8_regs_2bits / dq8_regs_3bits
symbols.contract: Register-resident window extraction for one lane's 8 codes of a 16x16 tile from TWO u32 words. 4-bit: FSHF_IMM(s, b, a, 20) then w7=b&0xffff, BFE16_IMM(w6,b,4)... w0=BFE16(s,8); words come from a lane shuffle: aw = __shfl_sync(mask, bw[t], (lane+31)&31). 2-bit: b = fshift(b, a, ((~t_offset)&8)<<1) with per-lane sources x_src_b = lane>>1, x_src_a = (i1+15)&15, two tiles per warp-load (tile t in lanes (t&1)*16..+15). 3-bit: per-lane precompute b1=(t_offset+257)*3, b2=b1+21, i0=(b1-16)/32, i2=(b2-1)/32, x_s2=(i2+1)*32-b2, sources i0%24 / i2%24, only lanes<24 load (LSTRIDE=24). All feed decode8<cb> -> two FragB (4x half2).
symbols.notes: The shared-memory-free extraction is the part most likely to break in a port; it is exercised end-to-end by the GEMV parity leg, and the tile-level ground truth is cpu_ref::decode_tile (row/col mapping row=(l%4)*2+(j&1)+((j>>1)&1)*8, col=((l&!4)/8)*2+((l>>2)&1)+((j>>2)&1)*8 for t=l*8+j).

symbols.name: mma_ab_h
symbols.contract: mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f16.f16.f16.f16 {%0,%1},{a01,a23},{b0,b1},{%0,%1} — A operand built from two FragB halves (rows = activations), fp16 accumulate in place. The GEMM path instead uses ptx_mma_m16n8k16(FragA, FragB, FragC) with f32 accumulators on sm_121a.
symbols.notes: Tensor-core-internal accumulation order for f16-acc is architecturally unspecified — do NOT attempt a bit-exact CPU replica of the GEMV dot products; that is what the tolerance gate is for.

symbols.name: EXL3_GEMM_ARGS / EXL3_MGEMM_ARGS / shape tables
symbols.contract: exl3_kernel_map.cuh: EXL3_GEMM_SHAPE_2..4 as above; EXL3_GEMM_TILESIZE_K {0,16,32,32,16}, TILESIZE_N {0,128,128,256,512}, BLOCKDIM {0,256,512,512,256}; EXL3_GEMM_BASE_THREADS 256; SMEM_MAX 90*1024. Host-side selection in Atlas replaces select_exl3_gemm_kernel/CoopKernelAutotuner: static per-shape choice + optional env override is enough for a fixed model.

symbols.name: DevCtx locks layout
symbols.contract: One zero-initialized int buffer per device: [0, MAX_TILES_C=1024*1024) tile locks; [MAX_TILES_C, +2*MAX_BARRIERS=1024) barrier counter+sense pairs for group_barrier; [MOE_SCHED_OFFSET, +MOE_SCHED_INTS) MoE scheduler ints. Port must allocate and zero this once per device (4*(1048576+2048+66) bytes ≈ 4.2 MB) and pass it to every launch; mgemm z-slice lock ranges are offset by blockIdx.z*size_n/128.
symbols.notes: Locks are self-resetting across launches (barrier_release final wave rewinds them); never re-zero between launches on a live stream.

symbols.name: exl3_gemv_cfg heuristic
symbols.contract: static int exl3_gemv_cfg(cc, m, k, n, K, cb, mode, narrow_coresident): eligibility K in [2,4], cb!=0 unless K==4, m<=8, k%128==0, n%128==0; narrow (CFG0) when size_n/32 <= narrow_coresident (one co-resident wave) or (k<=2048 && n<=8192); wide (CFG1) for n>=8192 && k<=4096. Ampere-tuned; upstream comment: 'Ada/Blackwell are memory-bound here and keep the regular kernel' (cc check commented out).
symbols.notes: For sm_121a treat the GEMV-vs-GEMM crossover as UNKNOWN: the bench binary must measure both paths at every m<=8 shape and the port should gate path choice on an env var + measured table, not the Ampere heuristic.

symbols.name: cpu_ref::decode_tile / reconstruct_had_f16 / reconstruct_had_bf16
symbols.contract: Existing Atlas oracle (crates/spark-runtime/src/weights/exl3.rs): decode_tile(packed 16*K u16, k, cb) -> [[f16;16];16] exact; reconstruct_had_f16 -> f16 [in,out] bits with the kernel's exact op order; reconstruct_had_bf16(gpu,...) -> device BF16 [out,in]. The matmul harness reuses decode_tile as the EXACT weight source for its f64 truth, and reconstruct_had_bf16 to build the materialized-path calibration arm.
symbols.notes: reconstruct's Hadamard stage math is fp16 (matching the reconstruct kernel) — that is a DIFFERENT rounding profile from the matmul kernels' fp32 rotation, which is why truth must be rebuilt in f64 from decode_tile rather than reusing reconstruct_had_f16.

symbols.name: exl3_matmul_parity (new example binary)
symbols.contract: crates/spark-model/examples/exl3_matmul_parity.rs, conventions cloned from exl3_reconstruct_parity.rs (Lcg seed 0x5EED_CAFE-style, up/down_u16 helpers, per-leg println table, EXL3_REAL_DIR real-tensor leg, exit 0=pass / 1=fail-or-vacuous-control / 2=kernels-absent probe on gpu.kernel("exl3_matmul", "exl3_gemv_k4_cb2_m1_cfg0")-style name). LEGS: (A) had128-exact: GPU input-rotation kernel (bf16->fp16 A_had) and output-rotation kernel vs CPU f32-order replicas, bit-identical required, shapes m in {1,8} x len in {128, 2560, 640}, random suh/svh (0.5..1.5 magnitude, random sign) + real suh.bin/svh.bin. (B) gemv m in {1,2,4,8}: shapes [2560->640] and [2560->6144], K in {2,3,4} x cb in {1,2} synthetic + REAL leg ([2560x640] K=4 cb2 from .research/real_tensor), both CFG 0/1 forced; gate rel_rms <= 8e-3 and max_z <= 4e-2 vs f64 truth. (C) gemm m in {16, 64, 128} same shapes + [2560->10240], c_fp32=true; gate rel_rms <= 2.5e-3, max_z <= 1.5e-2. (D) mgemm: 16 allocated experts [2560->640], B_indices selecting 10, fp16 B_weights summing to 1, num_tokens in {1,4}, c_fp32; per-token gates as (B)/(C) by m, truth = f64 sum of weighted per-expert products. (E) determinism: legs B and C run twice -> outputs bit-identical (fixed grid). (F) NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each must FAIL its gate: one whole tile's 16*K trellis words set to 0xFFFF; one 128-col block of svh doubled; cb decoded as 1 while data is cb2. Plus the calibration print: err(bf16-materialized path vs same truth) per leg, and assert err_native <= 2*err_materialized + 1e-3 on all fp32 legs (backstop, not the primary gate).
symbols.notes: f64 truth per leg: x ~ N(0,1) fp16 inputs; y64 = R_out^{f64}( R_in^{f64}(x_fp16_exact) @ What_f16_exact ) with What from cpu_ref::decode_tile and R = (H128/sqrt(128)) x diag(s) in f64. Metrics per output row: rel_rms = ||y_gpu - y64||2 / ||y64||2; max_z = max_i |y_gpu_i - y64_i| / RMS(y64).

read:parity-bench-design.dtype_notes: Kernel A/A_had/suh/svh are STRICTLY fp16 (half); Atlas activations are BF16, so the port's input-rotation kernel must load BF16, do the (already-fp32) rotation math, and store fp16 into A_had — zero extra rounding cost since the kernel converts to fp32 internally anyway; the output-rotation kernel symmetrically reads the matmul's C (fp16 or fp32) and stores BF16 (or FP32 for the residual highway). C dtype: c_fp32 template selects fp32 vs fp16 output AND, critically, the precision of the GEMM path's inter-block partial-sum round-trips through global memory (fp16 handoffs when c_fp32=false: '__floats2half2_rn(frag_c[n][0], frag_c[n][1])') and of the mgemm final expert reduction (a chained __hadd fp16 sum when c_fp32=false). Recommend c_fp32=true for all Atlas serving legs and convert to BF16 in the output rotation. Accumulators: GEMM path = fp32 MMA accumulation on sm_121a (EXL3_GEMM_H_ACC is '#if __CUDA_ARCH__ == 860' only); GEMV path = fp16 MMA accumulation by design, folded to fp32 every FOLD (4 or 2) k-slices — max ~64 fp16-accumulated k-elements per fold window. Tolerance derivation (u16 = 2^-11 = 4.88e-4, u_bf16 = 2^-8 = 3.9e-3): fp32-acc legs vs f64 truth at k=2560 — error sources are A_had fp16 storage (~u16 rms per element), fp32 adds (2^-24*sqrt(2560) ~ 3e-6, negligible), output store rounding (~u16); random-sign dot products keep the RMS-relative error roughly k-independent at O(u16), expected 5e-4..1e-3 -> gate rel_rms <= 2.5e-3 (3-5x margin), max_z <= 1.5e-2. fp16-acc GEMV legs — per fold window ~4 fp16 C-roundings against partials of up to 64 terms gives ~2u16*sqrt(64)*sqrt(40 windows)/sqrt(2560) ~ 1e-3..3e-3 extra rms; upstream's own measurement (exl3_gemm_inner.cuh): 'Max observed error vs fp32 accumulation is ~1% of output RMS at k=4096, well below quantization noise' -> gate rel_rms <= 8e-3, max_z <= 4e-2. Calibration backstop: the bf16-materialized reference path carries u_bf16 weight rounding (~4e-3..8e-3 rel RMS vs the same truth), so native-fp32 legs should measurably BEAT the materialized path; assert err_native <= 2*err_materialized + 1e-3 on fp32 legs. Negative controls sized to clear the gates decisively: a whole corrupted tile (16 columns, O(1) weight error) yields rel_rms >> 8e-3; a doubled 128-col svh block yields ~1.0 in that block; single-bit flips are reserved for the bitwise 'output changed' check (their gate-level signal, ~|dw|/(sqrt(k)*rms(w)) ~ 2e-2, is too close to the GEMV gate to be a reliable gate-control).
read:parity-bench-design.blackwell_notes: sm_121a (CC_BLACKWELL=5 in devctx terms) takes these branches: (1) EXL3_GEMM_H_ACC = 0 -> exl3_gemm_kernel accumulates MMA in fp32 (the fp16-acc trick is sm_86-only); (2) exl3_mgemm's per-iteration sync uses group_barrier(blockIdx.z, gridDim.x, locks + BARRIER_LOCKS_OFFSET) under '#if __CUDA_ARCH__ > 890', not grid.sync — z-groups (concurrent experts) proceed independently; (3) the GEMV heuristic's arch gate is commented out but its tuning is Ampere-measured ('Ada/Blackwell are memory-bound here and keep the regular kernel') — treat GEMV eligibility on GB10 as an open empirical question for the bench, not a given. Shared memory: dynamic SMEM_MAX = 90 KB needs cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize) opt-in; fits under sm_121a's ~99 KB per-block cap with the standard carveout. Cooperative launch: upstream launches everything via cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel; grid.sync is used ONLY around the fused rotation stages, so the Atlas port should split into three plain launches (rotate-in kernel -> matmul kernel -> rotate-out kernel; the GEMM path can keep its fused shmem_out_had epilogue and skip the third launch) and drop cooperative launch entirely — but the GEMM inner's spin-lock cross-block reduction still requires all blocks co-resident, so keep grid <= occupancy*num_SMs exactly as upstream computes it. All instruction primitives are supported on sm_121a: mma.m16n8k16 f16.f16 (fp16 and fp32 acc), cp.async, ldmatrix, __dp4a, __ldcs, funnel shifts, warp shuffles. Graph capture: launches are stateless w.r.t. the locks buffer (self-resetting), so decode-graph capture is possible later, but per the qwen4exp graph-capture playbook keep the harness graph-free.
read:parity-bench-design.port_plan: Copy verbatim: ptx.cuh, exl3_dq.cuh, codebook.cuh, hadamard_inner.cuh (minus the unused gated-MLP fusion if desired), the bodies of exl3_gemv_kernel.cuh / exl3_gemm_inner.cuh / exl3_gemm_kernel.cuh, the shape-table macros from exl3_kernel_map.cuh, and the locks-layout constants from exl3_devctx.cuh, into kernels/gb10/common/exl3_matmul.cu compiled to a new 'exl3_matmul' PTX module. Replace: all ATen host code with Rust (Exl3Weight already resolves trellis/suh/svh/K/cb from the store); DevCtx with a per-backend once-allocated zeroed locks buffer (~4.2 MB); the autotuner with a static shape choice (SHAPE_2 for n=640, SHAPE_3/4 for n>=6144, measured once on gx10) plus an env override; cooperative launch with three plain launches (new extern C entry points below), keeping grid = min(slices, occupancy-capped SMs). New kernels to write (thin wrappers over the verbatim device code): exl3_had_r128_in_bf16 (BF16 x -> fp16 A_had, pre_scale=suh), exl3_had_r128_out_{bf16,f32} (C -> rotated+svh-scaled BF16/FP32), and BF16 I/O shims on the gemv/gemm entry points. extern C entry points (one PTX symbol per template instance, named like the reconstruct module): exl3_gemv_k{2,3,4}_cb{1,2}_m{0,1}_cfg{0,1}[_f32], exl3_gemm_shape{2,3,4}_k{2,3,4}_cb{1,2}[_f32], exl3_mgemm_shape{2,3,4}_k{2,3,4}_cb{1,2}_f32, exl3_had_r128_{in,out}_*. VERIFICATION (the core of this task): stage 1 — bit-exact sub-oracles: (a) tile decode is already gated by exl3_reconstruct_parity (keep it green); (b) new had128 leg: rotation kernels vs a CPU f32 replica of had_hf_r_128_inner's exact op order (fp16 pre-scale mul, fp32 butterfly, 5 XOR shuffle stages sign-own-then-add, fp32 *0.088388347648f, one _rn rounding) — must be bit-identical, this pins the rotation before any tolerance question exists; (c) determinism leg: every native config launched twice must be bit-identical (fixed grid, lock-ordered reduction — any diff means a race). Stage 2 — tolerance-gated end-to-end oracle vs a CPU f64 truth pipeline (decode_tile weights, f64 rotations, f64 matmul), gates from dtype_notes: fp32-acc legs rel_rms<=2.5e-3 / max_z<=1.5e-2, fp16-acc GEMV legs rel_rms<=8e-3 / max_z<=4e-2, calibrated against the bf16-materialized arm (err_native <= 2*err_mat + 1e-3 on fp32 legs). Stage 3 — negative controls that must FAIL the gates (corrupted tile, doubled svh block, wrong codebook) so the harness can never go vacuous, mirroring exl3_reconstruct_parity's control convention. Stage 4 — bench binary vs the NVFP4 materialized path with the ship/flag/park criterion (<=1.15x ship, <=1.5x env-flag fidelity option, else park) and the memory table. Order of implementation: had128 kernels + leg A first (exact, fast to debug), then GEMV m=1 (smallest surface), then GEMM, then mgemm.
risks: GEMM inner spin-lock reduction deadlocks if the grid is not fully co-resident — the port must keep upstream's occupancy-capped grid computation exactly, and never launch these kernels concurrently with other work that evicts co-residency assumptions

mgemm A_had scratch undersizing is silent OOB corruption (upstream comment says 'found the hard way'); Rust host must assert bszm*m*k capacity, and the harness's mgemm leg should run under compute-sanitizer once

The Ampere-tuned GEMV heuristic may be wrong on GB10 (upstream expects Blackwell to prefer the regular kernel); shipping the wrong path costs decode latency silently — path choice must come from the bench table, and the parity harness must force-run BOTH paths so the unused one stays correct

fp16 C handoffs (c_fp32=false) add roundings in the GEMM inter-block reduction and turn the mgemm expert sum into a chained fp16 __hadd — using fp16 legs in serving would loosen the derived tolerances; the plan pins c_fp32=true and converts to BF16 in the rotation epilogue

Tolerance gates are derived for random N(0,1) inputs; real activations with outlier channels raise the constant — the REAL-tensor leg plus a real-activation capture leg (dump one qwen4_exp layer input) should be added before flipping the serving default
size_k must divide TILESIZE_K and size_n must divide TILESIZE_N per shape — a shape-selection bug at an unusual dim would read OOB; host-side ensure!() on divisibility per selected shape

lm_head [2560 x 248320] tiles_n up to 1940: locks indexing (MAX_TILES_C = 1M) is fine, but the m<=8 GEMV grid caps at co-residency and loops groups — verify the group loop ('for (int group = blockIdx.x; group < num_groups; group += gridDim.x)') covers n=248320 correctly in the parity harness (include an lm_head-width leg at reduced k if memory-tight)

Negative-control sizing: single-bit flips are near the GEMV gate threshold — controls use whole-tile corruption at gate level and keep single-bit flips only for bitwise-difference checks, else the vacuity check itself flakes

Clean-merge/toolchain hazard from memory: building all ATLAS_TARGET_MODEL targets is required or the new PTX module silently drops out of some target sets (the parity example's exit-2 probe exists precisely to catch this — CI must treat exit 2 as failure for qwen3.8-flash-next targets)
